items.title: L'ancien Premier ministre britannique appelle son pays à combattre la Russie dans l'Arctique
items.description: Dans un article publie dans The Sunday Times , l'ancien Premier ministre britannique Rishi Sunak a declare que Londres devait montrer que le pays etait capable de s'opposer a l'infrastructure militaire russe presente en Arctique afin de contenir le president russe Vladimir Poutine et empecher Moscou de renforcer davantage ses positions dans la region. Il a attire l'attention sur l'activite des navires russes et la vulnerabilite des infrastructures sous-marines. a l'appui de son argumentation, l'ex-Premier ministre britannique a cite les avertissements du ministre britannique de la Defense et du Premier Lord de la Mer, selon lesquels l'activite des forces navales russes au large des cotes britanniques a augmente de 41 % en un an. Rishi Sunak a accorde une importance particuliere, pour la securite du Royaume-Uni, a la peninsule de Kola, ou est basee la Flotte du Nord russe, en qualifiant cette region de source majeure de menace militaire pour le pays. Selon lui, le fait que Moscou prenne conscience de la vulnerabilite de ses installations face aux forces britanniques pourrait reduire le risque d'escalade. L'ancien Premier ministre a egalement averti que la perte du controle de l'Atlantique Nord pourrait compliquer le deploiement des troupes et du materiel americains en Europe. a cet egard, il a appele a renforcer la surveillance sous-marine et a elargir la cooperation militaire avec les allies d'Europe du Nord. Sunak a souligne que le Royaume-Uni ferait partie des rares pays capables de mener des operations militaires dans l'Arctique, rappelant notamment l'existence d'unites du Corps des marines britanniques entraînees pour operer dans des conditions climatiques extremes. Il a estime que la menace pesant sur l'infrastructure militaire russe permettrait de reduire le risque d'une nouvelle escalade du conflit, se declarant convaincu que la dissuasion de la Russie dans l'Arctique constituerait la contribution la plus importante du Royaume-Uni a la securite europeenne au cours des dix prochaines annees. Londres penche pour la confrontation, Moscou reaffirme son ouverture au dialogue Le Royaume-Uni est l'un des pays occidentaux les plus agressifs a l'egard de la Russie. En novembre, le chef d'etat-major de la defense britannique, Richard Knighton, a fait part de l'intention de Londres, en collaboration avec neuf etats europeens, de renforcer la surveillance des sous-marins russes dans l'Atlantique Nord, dans l'Arctique et en mer Baltique, en mobilisant la coordination des actions des forces navales, aeriennes et terrestres dans ces regions. Nikolaï Patrouchev, conseiller du president russe, a egalement fait etat de la preparation d'un blocus de la mer Baltique. Ainsi, en octobre dernier, lors de negociations avec le ministre chinois des Transports, Liu Wei, il a averti que les pays occidentaux tentaient d'organiser l'interception de navires russes. Dans le meme temps, les hauts responsables militaires britanniques comprennent la necessite d'etablir des contacts avec Moscou dans le domaine militaire. Le 10 novembre, le ministre britannique de la Defense, Wes Streeting, a appele a une telle demarche, en soulignant son importance pour limiter le risque de decisions erronees susceptibles d'entraîner une escalade. La Russie a quant a elle exprime a plusieurs reprises sa volonte de renouer le dialogue avec les pays europeens, malgre les tensions persistantes liees au conflit en Ukraine. En mai dernier, le porte-parole du Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, a declare que « les Russes sont prets a discuter », estimant que la voie de la negociation etait preferable a une confrontation generale.

items.title: Gideon Boako demands accountability over Mahama’s collapsed $10bn projects
items.description: Tano North MP Dr Gideon Boako has challenged President John Dramani Mahama’s government to account for previous US$10 billion project commitments, particularly the controversial STX housing deal. In a write-up issued on Sunday, November 15, Dr Boako argued that Ghana must establish what happened to resources committed to earlier projects before accepting fresh promises under the government’s New Economy Programme. He cited the STX housing project, announced in 2009 with an ambitious target of constructing 200,000 housing units within five years. According to him, Parliament approved an initial US$1.5 billion tranche for 30,000 housing units for the security services in August 2010, with a sod-cutting ceremony subsequently held at the Tesano Police Training Depot on January 27, 2011. However, the project collapsed following disagreements between STX Korea and its Ghanaian partner, GKA Airports Company, leaving the country without the promised housing units. Dr Boako alleged that Ghana was left with financial liabilities, with critics estimating losses of more than US$300 million, including US$245 million in political risk insurance payments. He recalled that then Vice President Mahama, who had been directly involved in efforts to secure the deal, announced its collapse on December 30, 2011. The MP also referenced the Hope City project, announced in 2013, and the US$10 billion Big Push infrastructure commitment, which featured in the NDC’s 2020 manifesto. He argued that the latest US$10 billion New Economy Programme follows a familiar pattern of ambitious announcements without sufficient evidence of implementation. “That is the definition of hoax political rhetoric – bold numbers with no funding, no financing structure, no investor list, no Act of Parliament. Just consultations,” he wrote. Dr Boako insisted that the government must provide clarity on the financing arrangements, investors and accountability mechanisms for its latest economic programme. “Ghana does not need another $10 billion city in the sky. Ghana needs the $10 billion already announced to be accounted for. Starting with STX,” he stated.

items.title: NAIMOS intensifies crackdown on illegal sand winning in Ketu North
items.description: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), with support from the Artillery Brigade of the Ghana Army, has carried out a major enforcement operation against suspected illegal sand-winning activities in the Ketu North Municipality of the Volta Region. The operation targeted two identified sites at Agbozume Klikor and Ohawu, where active sand-winning operations were disrupted as part of efforts to protect the environment and restore compliance within the sand extraction sector. During the operation, 30 persons were arrested, and 35 tipper trucks were intercepted. A significant number of the trucks were reported to bear Togolese registration numbers, raising further concerns about the movement of vehicles involved in sand-winning activities within the area. The arrested suspects were handed over to the Dzodze District Police Station for further investigation, while the intercepted trucks were moved to a secure holding location. For NAIMOS, the exercise sends a clear message that illegal sand winning will be treated with the same seriousness as other forms of unauthorised mineral extraction. Unregulated sand winning can degrade farmland, damage roads and surrounding landscapes, threaten communities, and undermine efforts to manage natural resources responsibly. NAIMOS has therefore warned that enforcement will not focus solely on those found excavating sand. Truck owners, transporters, and other actors who facilitate the movement of sand from unauthorised sites will also come under scrutiny if their activities are found to support illegal operations. The Secretariat will continue targeted operations in identified hotspots and maintain close collaboration with the Ghana Armed Forces, Ghana Police Service, local authorities and other relevant institutions to prevent the resurgence of illegal sand-winning activities. NAIMOS is urging operators in the sector to ensure that sand is sourced only from lawfully approved locations and that all activities are conducted in accordance with the relevant regulatory requirements. The message is clear: economic activity cannot be pursued at the expense of the environment and the law. NAIMOS will continue to act against illegal sand-winning operations and the logistics that sustain them, while supporting lawful and responsible operators.

items.title: Francophonie : Le troisième mandat de Louise Mushikiwabo divise les États membres
items.description: Réunis à Phnom Penh, au Cambodge, pour le 20e Sommet de la Francophonie qui se tient les 15 et 16 novembre 2026 , les chefs d’État et de gouvernement doivent se prononcer sur l’avenir de l’organisation. La possible reconduction de la Rwandaise Louise Mushikiwabo à la tête de l’OIF suscite de vives divergences, notamment en raison des tensions entre Kigali et Kinshasa. L’unité de la Francophonie mise à l’épreuve. Ouvert ce 15 novembre 2026 à Phnom Penh, le 20e Sommet de l’Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) se tient dans un contexte de tensions autour de la succession de sa Secrétaire générale, Louise Mushikiwabo. La question de son éventuel troisième mandat divise les États membres, traditionnellement attachés au principe du consensus. Soutenue par le président rwandais Paul Kagame, présent au sommet, la candidature de la Secrétaire générale sortante reste contestée. Louise Mushikiwabo estime toutefois être légitime à briguer un nouveau mandat, aucun texte de l’organisation ne l’interdisant. En cas d’absence de consensus, les États membres de plein droit pourraient recourir au vote pour départager les candidats. La crise entre le Rwanda et la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) pèse particulièrement sur les discussions. Kinshasa menace de quitter l’OIF si la Rwandaise est reconduite. Après le retrait de la candidature de Juliana Lumumba, la RDC soutient désormais celle de l’ancien Premier ministre roumain Dacian Cioloș. La Mauritanienne Coumba Bâ figure également parmi les prétendants. Ces divisions s'ajoutent au retrait du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger, qui reprochent à l'organisation des ingérences politiques. Dans ce contexte, le président sénégalais Bassirou Diomaye Faye aurait entrepris, selon des sources diplomatiques, de réunir ses homologues africains pour harmoniser leurs positions. Au-delà de ces enjeux institutionnels, les travaux portent sur le thème : « Réinvestir dans la paix pour une prospérité partagée et une stabilité durable ». Le Cambodge, qui accueille le premier sommet organisé en Asie du Sud-Est depuis celui de Hanoï en 1997, rappelle, à travers son histoire marquée par les conflits et la reconstruction, la fragilité de la paix. Les dirigeants sont notamment appelés à prendre des engagements dans les domaines de l’éducation, de la jeunesse, de la culture, de l’égalité entre les femmes et les hommes, du numérique et de la gouvernance démocratique. À un an de la fin de la programmation 2024-2027, ils devront également évaluer les résultats de l’organisation et adopter la Déclaration de Phnom Penh. El Hadji Gorgui Wade NDOYE

items.title: Mfantsipim @150: MOBA’96 donates to Cape coast hospital pre-term babies unit
items.description: The Child Health Unit of the Cape coast Teaching Hospital has received a boost in healthcare delivery after the 1996 Old Boys year group of Mfantsipim School made a kind donation to the hospital. The donation forms part of the year group’s commitment to giving back to society and supporting healthcare delivery, especially for vulnerable newborns who require specialised medical attention and care during the critical early stages of life. The cash donation of GH¢22,000, together with the incubator, is expected to contribute to improving the care and support available to pre-term babies at the hospital. The donation is to support awareness on pre-maturity by equipping the healthcare professionals with adequate resources to execute their mandate in reaching out to communities about the condition. As the lead sponsoring year group for the school’s Speechday celebration,President of MOBA’96, Kwesi Enchill, says the gesture was part of the Mfantsipim School Sesquicentennial celebrations to support healthcare delivery in a region that holds much of significance to the group’s formative years of education and development. He says the group was motivated to support the awareness creation of children born pre-maturely and allaying stigma and fears parents of such babies face. “We found that this issue was particularly about awareness and if this gesture is what would make people be in tune, then it’s a call in the right direction,” he said. Premature babies often require specialised equipment, constant monitoring and dedicated medical care to overcome the challenges associated with early birth. The contribution by the Class of 1996 is therefore a meaningful intervention that will support the hospital’s efforts to provide quality care to these vulnerable infants. The 25-bed capacity neonatal intensive care unit of the hospital has a majority of its admissions being pre-term babies. Head of the child health unit at Cape coast teaching hospital, Dr. Yemah Mariama Bukari, expressed their unit’s profound gratitude to the MOBA’96. She highlighted that the gesture would greatly contribute to the quality of care offered to the babies and enhance awareness to reach more communities.

items.title: Former APC spokesman warns of crisis if Tinubu is imposed in 2027
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Former Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the ruling All Progressives Congress APC, Timi Frank, has warned that any attempt to force President Bola Tinubu back into office in 2027 could plunge the country into crisis. Frank, who is the Ambassador to East Africa and the Middle East of the United Liberation Movement for West Papua (ULMWP), said Nigerians would not accept an outcome that contradicts their votes. “Nigerians will not accept a situation in which someone is declared the winner when the people know they did not vote for him. They should not push the country into a crisis by attempting to impose him on the people,” Frank warned. He urged the president to abandon his re-election ambition and guarantee a transparent electoral process. “Whoever wins should be allowed to emerge as the choice of the people,” he said. Frank also expressed concern over alleged attempts by some political actors to manipulate the electoral process. He described the public protest against Tinubu after prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in Area 1, Garki, Abuja, last Friday as evidence of growing dissatisfaction with the administration. Tinubu reportedly faced boos from some Hausa protesters who chanted “Ba ma yi” (we don’t want you) after the prayers. In a viral video, some protesters were seen removing and destroying his campaign posters and billboards in parts of Area 1. Frank condemned the protesters for choosing a religious occasion to vent their displeasure and commended the President’s security detail for ensuring his safety and de-escalating the situation. He nevertheless urged the President to recognise the significance of the public reaction. “The rejection was total and unmistakable. No Nigerian president has been embarrassed like this publicly. The way Nigerians rejected him speaks volumes but should he decide to go ahead and he loses, he should be prepared to accept defeat just like former President Goodluck Jonathan did,” he said. The former APC spokesman said he was worried by what he called a growing gap between the assurances given to the President by political associates and the mood of the people. “I have seen the confidence with which some people are assuring President Tinubu that he will win the Federal Capital Territory FCT and that he is firmly in control. But the reported embarrassment he suffered during a prayer session in Abuja tells a different story. “What happened in the FCT last Friday showed that political assurances and promises are not necessarily a reflection of the reality on the ground. The public reaction reflects the anger and dissatisfaction of Nigerians, which those around the President may not be telling him about. “What happened in FCT and Jos after the APC rally has shown that people like the FCT minister, Nyesom Wike promising him 80 percent of votes in Abuja and the Governor of Edo State, Monday Okpebholo vowing to give him 2.5 million votes in Edo state, would disappoint him due to the reality on ground. “Those telling him to continue and assuring him that he will win the next election are merely deceiving him. Even some people within his political circle, including those involved in his campaign, know that selling his candidacy to Nigerians will be difficult,” Frank said. He alleged that financial considerations were influencing the positions of some political associates, and said the President needed honest assessments of his performance and popularity. “I am giving him this advice because I genuinely want him to listen to the truth. Those around him may not be telling him that he has become very unpopular and that continuing in the presidential race may be a difficult undertaking. My advice is that he should take a bow and leave the race. He should take this advice seriously,” he said. Frank urged Tinubu to take a cue from opposition figures, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State governor, Peter Obi, whom he said draw large crowds without financial inducements. “Wherever these opposition leaders go, Nigerians come out in large numbers to receive them without being induced with rice or money. Their reception should tell the President something about the mood of the country,” he said. He listed hunger, unemployment, rising living costs and insecurity among the factors fuelling public anger. “If the President had performed well, there would be no need for the desperation we are witnessing today,” he said. Frank also questioned the credibility of endorsements for the President, alleging that some individuals and groups were motivated by anticipated financial benefits rather than genuine public sentiment. “President Tinubu still has an opportunity to make history and have his name written in gold. He can achieve this by ensuring that the country conducts a free, fair and credible election,” he said. items.title: Agbodza raises concerns over vote-buying, conduct in NDC constituency elections
items.description: The Minister of Roads and Highways, Kwame Governs Agbodza, has expressed concern over the conduct of some party members during recent constituency-level elections of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), warning that certain practices risk undermining the party’s values and political identity. Addressing party faithful, Mr Agbodza said he had observed incidents during the electoral process that reminded him of practices he would ordinarily associate with the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP). He said he was particularly troubled by what he witnessed across the Volta Region and other parts of the country, insisting that the party needed to reflect on its conduct and make the necessary corrections. The minister disclosed that he had never paid anyone a cedi to influence the outcome of an election in his Adaklu constituency, suggesting that he was uncomfortable with practices involving the use of money to secure political support. “I have never paid a cedi to anybody in Adaklu directed branch at the constituency election before. At the past elections, we saw things like that happen. You can say that is good,” he said. Mr Agbodza indicated that some of the developments he witnessed during the latest elections were particularly disappointing, given the political tradition and identity of the NDC. “Yesterday, I saw things that I actually thought it was NPP people doing it. Today, you may be happy about it,” he stated. He stressed that the concerns were not limited to his constituency, but reflected observations he had made across the Volta Region and other parts of Ghana. “I am saying what I saw yesterday across the region, across the country. This is not the Rawlings party. I can’t say more. Let’s keep it. Let’s reflect on it, and let’s make amendments,” he added. Mr Agbodza also criticised the tendency among politicians to avoid speaking frankly about internal party challenges for fear of offending colleagues or losing their affection. He said he was prepared to express his concerns regardless of whether his comments would make him popular among party members. “In our part of the world, when we see trouble, because everybody wants to be loved, somehow I don’t really care whether somebody like me or not. I don’t know why I’m like that. I am 24 years. If I don’t have enough friends now, I don’t need more,” he said. He urged party members to examine the conduct of the recent constituency elections, acknowledge practices that could damage the party’s reputation and take steps to address them.

items.title: NGE demands release of detained investigative journalist, Ojukwu
items.description: The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has condemned the arrest, detention and prosecution of Daniel Ojukwu, an investigative journalist with the Foundation for Investigative Journalism (FIJ), demanding his immediate release on bail. The Guild also called for a review of the criminal charges against Ojukwu and FIJ founder, Fisayo Soyombo, warning that the prosecution could undermine press freedom and discourage investigative journalism in Nigeria. Ojukwu is currently being held at the Kuje Correctional Centre, Abuja, after being arraigned on a 12-count charge bordering on alleged cyberstalking and criminal defamation. In a statement dated November 15 and signed by its President, Eze Anaba, and General Secretary, Onuoha Ukeh, the NGE said it was alarmed that a journalist was facing criminal prosecution over reports raising questions about the expenditure of public funds by the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Sustainable Development Goals. The Guild said Ojukwu’s investigation reportedly exposed an alleged payment of more than ₦147 million, approximately $109,000, to an Abuja-based restaurant for the construction of classrooms and a skills acquisition centre at a primary school in Lagos. According to the NGE, the investigation raised questions about the existence of the projects, as well as the capacity and track record of the company involved in the contract. It described the issues raised by the investigation as legitimate matters of public accountability that deserved transparent answers rather than the prosecution of the journalist who brought them to public attention. The Guild expressed particular concern that Ojukwu had been remanded in prison despite pleading not guilty to the charges, while his bail application, initially scheduled for November 12, was adjourned until December 1. It said the resort to arrest, detention and criminal prosecution over journalistic work raised concerns about the commitment of authorities to press freedom, freedom of expression and Nigerians’ constitutional right to information. The NGE recalled its opposition to the alleged use of cybersecurity laws by the police and other security agencies to harass, intimidate and bully journalists. “Investigative journalism is not a crime. Asking questions about public expenditure is not cyberstalking. Demanding accountability from public officials is not defamation,” the Guild said. It maintained that public office holders must be open to scrutiny over their management of public resources, adding that journalists should not face threats of arrest, prosecution or imprisonment for reporting alleged irregularities. While acknowledging the right of individuals to seek legal redress over publications they consider injurious to their reputation, the Guild warned against using such rights to intimidate journalists or suppress legitimate investigations. The organisation also warned that Ojukwu’s continued detention could have a chilling effect on investigative journalism, sending a message to journalists that scrutinising public expenditure could expose them to prosecution and imprisonment. Citing Sections 39 and 22 of the 1999 Constitution, the NGE said freedom of expression and the responsibility of the media to hold government accountable must be respected and upheld. The Guild consequently demanded Ojukwu’s immediate release on bail pending the determination of the charges, an end to intimidation and harassment of journalists, and transparent investigation and prosecution of allegations involving the misuse of public funds. It also called for a review of the charges against Ojukwu and Soyombo, taking into consideration constitutional guarantees of press freedom and the public interest served by investigative journalism. The NGE further urged the police and other law enforcement agencies to stop abusing cybersecurity laws and refrain from deploying criminal legislation to settle disputes arising from legitimate journalistic investigations. It called on the judiciary to protect fundamental rights and ensure that judicial processes were not used to silence critical voices. “The Guild will not stand by while freedom of the press is eroded through intimidation, harassment and the misuse of the criminal justice system,” the statement added. items.title: Blé français pour l’Algérie : de 8 millions de tonnes par an à « presque zéro »
items.description: Longtemps premiers fournisseurs de l’Algérie, les céréaliers français sont plus que doublés. La baisse des ventes de blé tendre de la France à l’Algérie est, en effet, spectaculaire depuis que les autorités algériennes se sont mises à diversifier les fournisseurs. La presse française évoque une « quasi-disparition » d’un « marché historique ». L’Office algérien interprofessionnel des céréales (OAIC), l’organisme public algérien chargé de l’importation de céréales, multiplie les appels d’offres sur le marché international, et il n’y a toujours pas de fournisseurs français qui sont retenus. Le volume des ventes de blé français à l’Algérie a fondu en quelques années La dernière opération en date concerne l’achat, entre le 9 et le 13 novembre, de plus de 700.000 tonnes de blé tendre , dont une grande partie devrait provenir d'Argentine, où, indique l'agence Reuters, « la nouvelle récolte débute, donnant lieu à des offres très compétitives sur les marchés d’exportation ». La Roumanie et la Bulgarie pourraient aussi figurer parmi les fournisseurs. Cet appel d’offres porte à 5,3 millions de tonnes de blé tendre achetées par l'Algérie depuis le début de l’année auprès de divers fournisseurs. Dans ce gros marché, la part des céréaliers français est réduite à presque rien. « Les exportations françaises vers l’Algérie, qui atteignaient plusieurs millions de tonnes par an, sont désormais proches de zéro », déplore le site français Action agricole Picardie. Citant les estimations de Thierry Pouch, économiste en chef des Chambres d’agriculture France, le média rappelle qu’entre 2018 et 2023, « la France expédiait chaque année quelque 6 à 8 millions de tonnes de blé tendre » vers l’Algérie. Aujourd'hui, les céréaliers français sont remplacés par d'autres fournisseurs. Blé : l’Ukraine fournit désormais près du tiers des importations de l’Algérie Alors que les échanges commerciaux entre la France et l’Algérie ne cessent de dégringoler, passant sous la barre des 9 milliards d’euros en glissement annuel, la filière céréalière est frappée de plein fouet. Il s’agit d’une retombée directe du changement des critères de l’Algérie qui permet au blé d'autres fournisseurs d'entrer sur son marché. Outre la crise politique, les fournisseurs français font les frais de la forte concurrence sur le marché. Parmi les nouveaux grands fournisseurs de blé à l’Algérie figure l’Ukraine. Selon l'ambassadeur de ce pays en Algérie, Oleksandr Voronin, qui a rencontré début novembre le ministre de l’Agriculture Sid Ali Khaldi, « environ 30 % des importations de céréales en Algérie proviennent de la production ukrainienne ». L’article Blé français pour l’Algérie : de 8 millions de tonnes par an à « presque zéro » est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: AFCON 2027: 6 countries who need a win to keep qualification hopes alive
items.description: Six countries are facing an uphill battle to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) after losing all three of their opening matches in the qualifying campaign. Lesotho, South Sudan, Somalia, Sierra Leone, Central African Republic and Liberia are yet to record a point after three rounds of matches, leaving them bottom of their respective groups . With three matchdays remaining, the six countries will need to turn their fortunes around quickly to stand a realistic chance of securing a place at the tournament. Lesotho occupy the bottom position in Group A after suffering three consecutive defeats. Their latest setback came against Gabon, who secured a 2-0 victory on Friday, November 13. The result left Lesotho without a point, while group leaders Morocco maintained their perfect record with a 5-1 victory over Niger to move to nine points. South Sudan are experiencing a similarly difficult campaign in Group B, having lost their third consecutive match following a 2-0 defeat to Angola on Saturday, November 14. The South Sudanese side are bottom of the group with zero points, eight behind joint leaders Egypt and Angola, who have both collected seven points. In Group C, Somalia are also struggling after losing 2-0 to Ghana on Thursday, November 12. The defeat marked their third straight loss, leaving them at the bottom without a point. Ivory Coast lead the group with nine points after beating Gambia 2-1, while Gambia remain second with six points. Sierra Leone are another country under pressure after losing all three of their opening fixtures in Group E. Their latest defeat came against DR Congo, who secured a 3-1 victory on Thursday, November 12, to maintain their position at the top of the group with nine points. Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea occupy second and third positions with four points each, while Sierra Leone remain bottom without a point. Central African Republic have also endured a disappointing start to their qualifying campaign in Group F. They suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat to Benin on Thursday, November 12, leaving them with three losses from three matches. Benin and Burkina Faso are joint leaders of the group with seven points each, while Mauritania occupy third position with three points. Liberia complete the list of six winless countries after losing 4-2 to Cape Verde on Friday, November 13. The defeat left Liberia bottom of Group K without a point, while Mali lead the group with nine points following their 3-2 victory over Rwanda. Rwanda are second with six points, while Cape Verde have three. Although the six countries have made difficult starts, none has been mathematically eliminated from the qualification race, with three rounds of matches still to be played. The fourth round of qualifiers begins on November 16, giving the struggling teams another opportunity to secure their first points and revive their campaigns. The 2027 AFCON qualifiers feature 48 countries divided into 12 groups. The top two teams in nine groups will qualify for the tournament, while only the highest-placed non-host country will qualify from Groups D, H and L. This is because Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania, the three co-hosts of the competition, have already secured automatic qualification. The 2027 Africa Cup of Nations will be jointly hosted by the three East African countries from June 19 to July 17, 2027. items.title: The Right Diagnosis, an Incomplete Cure: The 2027 Budget and Ghana’s Boom-and-Bust Cycles
items.description: “These boom-and-bust cycles must cease” On the evening of Thursday, November 12, 2026, the Minister for Finance, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, when presenting the 2027 budget told Parliament that Ghana’s boom-and-bust cycles must cease. Few Ghanaians would disagree. Too many times we have lived through hope followed by hardship, a stable cedi followed by sharp depreciation, and a recovery followed by another crisis. I have read the full 2027 Budget Statement, and I want to answer one question. Does the Minister appreciate why the boom-and-bust cycles happen, and does his New Economy programme remove the cause? My answer is that the Minister has made the right diagnosis but prescribed an incomplete cure. The budget sees two causes clearly. It misses a third, and the third is the one that will bring the next bust. What the budget gets right The budget statement is more candid about the causes of our instability than most budgets before it. It says the cedi came under pressure “when prices dropped or fiscal discipline weakened” (para. 161). It concedes that “temporary booms had financed permanent commitments” (para. 168), and it blames reckless spending, weak revenue and expensive debt for the crisis of 2022. Most important, the budget statement admits that past governments repaired the public finances “but did not use the recovery to alter the structure of the economy,” and so “the cycle began again” (paras. 186–187). It even pledges that fiscal discipline “will apply throughout the election cycle” (para. 239). So the Government does understand two causes: our dependence on raw commodity exports, and fiscal indiscipline. I accept both. My quarrel is with what is missing. The machine that is not in the plan Read the eight pillars of the New Economy and one thing stands out. The only imports the budget counts as a drain on the cedi are things we consume: rice, sugar, poultry, fish, vegetables and medicines. It says the food import bill “weakens the cedi” (para. 260). It promises that when Ghana grows and processes more, “the cedi will face less pressure” (para. 336). It demands that every cedi of fiscal space answer the question: “what imports will it replace?” (para. 191). The budget never asks that question of the factories themselves. Throughout the statement, machines are things to buy and finance: • the “manufacturer investing in new machinery” is offered equipment leasing (paras.228, 231); • the rice hubs receive tax incentives for “irrigation, mechanisation, silos, modern mills” (para. 276); • GH¢800 million is allocated “to procure agriculture machinery” (para. 1543); • the review of Chapter 98 of the Customs Tariff concerns duty concessions on imported “machinery and other inputs” (para. 860); • the textiles pillar promises jobs for machine operators, not machine makers (para. 448); • for the nuclear plant, “international partners will only provide technology, finance, engineering and specialist services” (para. 380). Cocoa grinding mills, gold refineries, alumina plants, rice mills, garment lines and pharmaceutical plants are all capital goods. Ghana makes almost none of them, and few of their spare parts. Every one will be imported and paid for in dollars, and every one will be kept running with imported spares, also paid for in dollars. The arithmetic The budget’s own figures show where the capacity to make machines stands in the Government’s order of priorities. 2027 allocation Amount New Economy programme, 2027 outlay (para. 249) GH¢30 billion Procurement of agricultural machinery (para. 1543) GH¢800 million Completion of the Foundry and Machine Tooling Centre (para. 1582) GH¢51 million GRATIS Foundation, whole year, no capital expenditure (Appendix 4A) about GH¢3 million The Foundry and Machine Tooling Centre is the one line in this budget about making machines rather than buying them. The Centre dates from my time as Minister for Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation, and six years after I left office it is still waiting to be completed. In 2027 it receives about 0.17 percent of the New Economy outlay, and one-sixteenth of what we will spend on imported farm machinery in the same year. GRATIS, built to carry engineering capability into the regions, receives less than half of one percent of the machinery budget. Nothing in the New Economy programme is set aside for machine tools, foundries, spare parts or engineering manufacturing. How the next bust will come Suppose the New Economy succeeds exactly as planned. By 2030 Ghana processes all its cocoa, refines all its gold, processes all its manganese and bauxite and mills its own rice. Food imports fall, export earnings per tonne rise, and the cedi strengthens. But each of those plants was built with imported equipment, and each needs a steady flow of imported spares, replacement parts and, in time, replacement machines. When a mill breaks down, it cannot wait for the cedi to recover. It must buy the part at whatever the exchange rate happens to be. This demand for foreign exchange is stubborn, and it grows with every factory we open. The budget itself names commodity price volatility as the first of its five principal risks (para. 1025). When commodity prices next fall, export earnings will drop, but the bill for machines and spares will not. The cedi will come under pressure again, and the cycle will begin again, at a higher level of output but under the same ceiling. That is the trap of an economy that assembles but does not make. Value addition on imported capital goods moves the bottleneck; it does not remove it. There is a fiscal test as well. The programme is financed partly by lowering the primary surplus target by one percentage point of GDP (para. 247), beginning in the year before an election. The Government will answer that a surplus of at least 0.5 percent of GDP remains (para. 221), and that is a fair answer. But the pledge of discipline “throughout the election cycle” will be tested in 2028, and Ghanaians have heard such pledges before. What a complete cure would require The modern world economy is knowledge-based and driven by science and technology. Societies that produce, adapt and commercialise knowledge have achieved sustained growth and rising living standards. Raising money to pay foreign contractors to build infrastructure, good as the projects may be, cannot by itself lead to sustained economic development. Ghana has to develop the capacity to build the machines its industries run on. The cure is not to abandon value addition. It is to add the pillar the plan lacks: the capacity to make the machines. Make capital goods a ninth pillar of the New Economy, with its own budget, targets and delivery unit, as the other eight have. Fund the Foundry and Machine Tooling Centre to operate, not merely to be completed, and link it to the processing enclaves as a supplier of spare parts. Establish the Design and Manufacturing Technology Centre called for at the conference of Ghanaian scientists and engineers that the Ministry of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation and the Ghana Institution of Engineering convened at Peduase in January 2019. The foundry can cast and machine parts; the Centre would let Ghana design the machines themselves, working with the processing enclaves on the equipment they need. Apply the budget’s own local-preference principle to machines. If public money spent on rice must buy Ghana rice (para. 283), public money spent on silos, mills, dryers and processing equipment should, where quality allows, buy from Ghanaian fabricators: Suame Magazine, the regional centres of GRATIS, KNUST’s Technology Consultancy Centre, and the private engineers who have already shown what they can do. Reform Chapter 98 so that duty concessions on imported machinery are matched by incentives to make the same machinery here, and are phased down as local capacity grows. Judge every New Economy project by its import content, not only by the jobs and exports it creates. The question every factory must answer The Minister asked every cedi of fiscal space to say which imports it will replace. I ask the same question of every factory the New Economy will build. Until Ghana can make at least some of the machines that make its goods, our booms will be paid for in dollars we will not have when the bust comes. The diagnosis in this budget is right. The cure is not yet complete. © 2026 Prof. Kwabena Frimpong-Boateng. items.title: Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026: Final-day shopping, unbeatable deals, live music await patrons at Ghud Park
items.description: The doors are open, the vendors are ready, the music is playing and the bargains are waiting, the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 has entered its final day, with patrons being urged to make their way to Ghud Park at Accra Mall today, Sunday, November 15, for one last opportunity to shop, discover exciting Ghanaian brands, enjoy live-band performances and take advantage of attractive prices. After two exciting days of business exhibitions, product displays, shopping, networking and thrilling musical performances, the three-day event is heading towards its grand finale, but there is still plenty of excitement to experience. For those who have not visited, today is the last opportunity to be part of the action. And for those who have already enjoyed the fair, there are more products to discover, more vendors to patronise and more entertainment to enjoy before the exhibition closes. With more than 80 brands and businesses showcasing their products and services, the fair has transformed Ghud Park into a vibrant marketplace where shopping meets entertainment and Ghanaian entrepreneurship takes centre stage. From food and beverages to fashion, beauty, electronics, agricultural produce, household essentials, technology, financial services and real estate, the exhibition offers an impressive variety of products and services under one roof. A shopping paradise with exciting bargains Whether you are looking to restock your kitchen, upgrade your wardrobe, purchase beauty essentials, find gifts for loved ones or discover innovative products, the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair has something for you. With participating businesses offering special deals, discounts and promotional prices, patrons have an opportunity to explore different products, compare prices and make purchases directly from the businesses behind the brands. Forget the stress of moving from one shopping destination to another. At Ghud Park, shoppers can explore a wide range of products, interact with business owners, ask questions and discover new brands in one convenient location. From everyday household necessities to premium lifestyle products, the variety on display makes the fair an attractive destination for individuals, families and business owners. And it is not just about buying products. Visitors can also learn about the businesses, understand how their products are made, discover new services and establish useful commercial connections. Food lovers are in for a treat If food is your motivation, there is every reason to make Ghud Park your destination today. The fair has brought together an exciting collection of food processors, beverage manufacturers, agricultural businesses, caterers and food vendors, offering patrons a chance to sample and purchase a wide variety of locally made products. Among the participating businesses are Wilmar Africa, showcasing its Fortune Spread brand; Kivo; Didi Shito; Corki Ventures; Adjoor Ventures; Manellah Foods; Gold Coast Foods, with its Sankofa Spices; Yaapee Royal Foods; Nutrismart Ventures; Golden Parani Company Limited; G-Way Investments Africa Limited; Ikam Plus Company Limited; and ESBONY Food Package. For those looking for refreshing drinks and alternative beverages, exhibitors include Koa Impact Commerce, showcasing natural cocoa juice; Delsoy Ltd, with soy milk; Orave Juices, offering fruit juice; Pinnacle Coco Limited, with coconut juice; Jussvina Drinks (Global 500); Green Cup, featuring beetroot, guava and pawpaw tea; and Myst Natural Water. BB Brothers is also showcasing its products, while Mushroom General brings processed mushroom products to the exhibition. Agricultural and fresh-produce enthusiasts can explore offerings from T&C Farms, Atohfield, Orrab Farms and Farm Mate, while Flourish Foods Africa is presenting grilled chicken and poultry products. The food experience extends to ready-to-eat meals and snacks, with MamsiJoy Ventures offering rice, Ellie Catering Services serving fufu, Martha’s Yam Trading specialising in yam, and Selis Satisfactory showcasing kenkey. Other food vendors include Di Dwa Foods, Bliss Pop, 97 Bakes, Aladdin Bakery, Evive Delight Ltd and Desco Ltd. From locally processed foods and fresh agricultural produce to beverages, spices, baked products and delicious Ghanaian meals, visitors have plenty of reasons to explore the food section. Patrons should come hungry, bring their shopping bags and take advantage of the opportunity to discover products that could become regular features in their homes. Fashion, beauty and lifestyle: Give yourself a treat Fashion lovers have not been left out. A variety of businesses are showcasing clothing, footwear, bags, accessories and other fashion products, giving shoppers an opportunity to refresh their wardrobes and discover new styles. Among the participating fashion brands are Haute Xklusive, La Robe Classique, Asangenta, Utonez Clothier, Kofikyere Klothing, Regy Couture Ltd, Kims Foods and Clothings, and JAT Couture. Shoes TE3 is presenting footwear for different sizes, while Kinky Love Crochet is showcasing hair products and wigs. Beauty and personal-care enthusiasts can also explore products from Haus of Lush, RNS Beauty, Leepoku Ventures, Atlas Prime Merchantile Ltd and Chocho. Mist and Strands is exhibiting bath and body products, while Reed Diffusers Ghana Ltd and Esquicet Scents are presenting home-fragrance products, including diffusers and scented candles. Liz Imports is also showcasing perfumes and home appliances, while Kemz Ceramics is bringing ceramic products to the exhibition. For those looking to brighten their spaces, Eldem Floral Services is exhibiting fresh-cut flowers. Businesses serving mothers, children and families are also represented, including Roses Enterprise, Mothercare and Prestige Children’s Palace. Whether you are searching for a new outfit, footwear, beauty products, fragrances or something special for the home, there is plenty to discover. Technology, electronics and household essentials The exhibition also provides an opportunity for technology enthusiasts and shoppers looking for practical household solutions. Galop Sea Limited is showcasing laptops and accessories, while Xfromo Hypermart is presenting mobile phones and accessories, including Google Pixel devices. Katon 360 Technologies is exhibiting a digital platform designed to support SMEs, while Solid Connect is showcasing an application for artisans. We Shop Africa and Ayuda are represented in the e-commerce sector, offering visitors an opportunity to explore digital shopping solutions. Those interested in vehicles can visit Atlantic Meridian EV, which is showcasing electric vehicles, while Vital Vendors is offering car essentials. For household and construction-related products, Sintex Tank is presenting water-storage solutions, DBS is showcasing housing and roofing products, and MGIG Suppliers is exhibiting powdered soap. Worafam Group of Companies is also showcasing safety wear, while Greenhaul Solutions is presenting its waste-management and scrap-procurement services. Other businesses at the fair include Vaal Real Estate, Advantage GH Premium Apparel, Blessed 3 Ventures, Gorgeous Vie Event Hub, Grandeur Consult Travel and Tour, Astolinks and Afram Publication. Visitors can also explore products and services from BB Chemist, which is showcasing its Relax Liver Salt product, and Golden Pride (Yao Consult). Major brands and institutions also represented The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 has attracted the participation of established institutions and major brands alongside emerging businesses. Ecobank, MTN, the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA), Glico Life and Central University are among the institutions participating in the exhibition. Their presence adds to the diversity of the fair, providing opportunities for visitors to learn about financial services, telecommunications, insurance, export promotion and educational opportunities. The combination of established institutions and smaller businesses reinforces the fair’s role as a meeting point for different segments of Ghana’s business community. Shopping meets music, dancing and entertainment But there is more to the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair than shopping. The event has become an entertainment destination in its own right, with musical performances and activities adding excitement to the exhibition. The second day ended on a particularly high note as Ghanaian music duo Lali X Lola and King Jerry treated patrons to lively performances that turned the exhibition grounds into a celebration of music and entrepreneurship. The atmosphere was infectious. Patrons sang along, danced and captured memorable moments, while some vendors temporarily left their stalls and even carried their products onto the dance floor. It was a remarkable sight, with business owners turning their merchandise into part of the celebration and demonstrating that promoting a business can be both productive and entertaining. Joy Prime’s KMJ and content creator Quecy Official also brought additional excitement to the opening-day activities, engaging exhibitors and patrons. Today, as the exhibition enters its final stretch, patrons can look forward to more entertainment, live-band performances and an enjoyable atmosphere as the fair prepares to draw the curtains on its 2026 edition. So, whether you are coming to shop, enjoy the music, spend time with friends or simply experience the atmosphere, Ghud Park is the place to be. A platform for Ghanaian businesses to grow Beyond the shopping and entertainment, the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair is an important platform for promoting Ghanaian entrepreneurship. Organised by the Multimedia Group in partnership with Ecobank and powered by JoyPrime, the initiative seeks to provide small and medium-sized enterprises with greater market access, brand visibility and opportunities to connect with potential customers and business partners. For participating businesses, the fair offers an opportunity to introduce their products to new audiences, increase sales, receive direct feedback from consumers and establish relationships that could support future growth. For shoppers, it provides an opportunity to discover local brands, interact directly with entrepreneurs and support businesses contributing to Ghana’s economy. The 2026 edition builds on the maiden fair held in October 2025, which attracted more than 160 exhibitors and recorded over 1,000 visitors on its opening day. The continued organisation of the exhibition reflects efforts to create a stronger connection between Ghanaian businesses and consumers while providing SMEs with opportunities to compete, grow and expand their market reach. If you have been postponing your visit, this is the moment to make good on that promise. Do not wait until the stalls are packed up, the music stops and the vendors begin preparing to leave before regretting missing out. Make your way to Ghud Park at Accra Mall today, Sunday, November 15, and experience the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 before it closes. Come ready to shop, discover, eat, dance and support Ghanaian businesses. Bring your family. Invite your friends. Come with your shopping list and be prepared to discover products you never knew you needed. Take advantage of the attractive prices and available promotional offers, enjoy the live-band performances, interact with the vendors and soak in the vibrant atmosphere. From delicious local foods and refreshing beverages to fashionable clothing, beauty products, electronics, household essentials and innovative business solutions, there is something for everyone. items.title: Sudan Customs: ‘Exemption for returnees’ household goods expired’
items.description: Sudan’s department of Customs has issued a statement reiterating that the customs duty exemption granted on household furniture and electrical appliances brought back by Sudanese citizens who fled abroad because of the war expired on 2 November. Sudan Customs has announced the expiry of the customs exemption granted to household furniture and electrical appliances belonging to Sudanese citizens who left the country because of the war. The exemption expired on 2 November. In a press statement on Thursday, Customs said the expired exemption applied specifically to Sudanese citizens who had left the country because of the war. It is separate from the customs exemptions granted to Sudanese working abroad when they return permanently to the country at the end of their period of employment overseas. Customs stressed that the expiry of the exceptional exemption does not mean that the regulations governing exemptions for the luggage, furniture, and electrical appliances of Sudanese returning permanently from abroad have been cancelled or suspended. It added that these procedures remain subject to the regulations and requirements issued by the authorities responsible for Sudanese citizens working abroad. Customs urged citizens to observe the applicable regulations when arranging their return and bringing in their luggage and personal belongings, and to contact the relevant customs authorities for the necessary information. items.title: COP31: le Maroc met en avant la sécurité hydrique comme levier majeur de l’adaptation climatique
items.description: Le ministère de l’Équipement, de l’Eau et des Forêts prend part à la 31ème Conférence des Parties à la Convention-cadre des Nations Unies sur les changements climatiques (COP31), qui se tient du 9 au 20 novembre à Antalya, avec pour objectif de mettre en avant l’engagement du Royaume en faveur de l’action climatique, particulièrement dans les domaines de l’adaptation et du renforcement de la résilience hydrique face aux effets du changement climatique. Dans un contexte marqué par la succession des épisodes de sécheresse et l’intensification des phénomènes climatiques extrêmes, le ministère poursuit la mise en œuvre d’une politique intégrée de gestion des ressources en eau, fondée notamment sur la diversification des ressources, la rationalisation de la demande ainsi que le renforcement des dispositifs de prévention et d’alerte face aux risques d’inondation, indique le département dans une déclaration de presse. Cette participation constitue également une occasion de valoriser l’expérience marocaine, notamment à travers la contribution du ministère aux panels de haut niveau et aux événements parallèles consacrés à l’adaptation et à la résilience climatique. Elle vise, en outre, à consolider les partenariats internationaux, à promouvoir le partage d’expertise et à favoriser la mobilisation des financements et des solutions innovantes nécessaires à la concrétisation des projets d’adaptation. À travers sa participation à cette conférence, le ministère réaffirme que la sécurité hydrique constitue un enjeu majeur de l’adaptation au changement climatique et une condition essentielle du développement durable et de la résilience des territoires. The post COP31: le Maroc met en avant la sécurité hydrique comme levier majeur de l’adaptation climatique appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Open Street Fair pushes for people-centred road infrastructure in Accra
items.description: The Founder of Transform Transport Accra, Nii Noi Omaboe, is calling for a rethinking of how streets in Ghanaian cities are designed and used, insisting that road infrastructure should serve more than just vehicular traffic. He says streets should provide spaces for walking, cycling, recreation, artistic expression and community interaction. He made the call during an interview on the sidelines of the Open Street Fair organised by Transform Transport Accra at Abelemkpe, on Saturday, November 14. The event temporarily closed the stretch to vehicular traffic, allowing participants to reclaim the road through activities including cycling, skating, walking, graffiti painting, floor art and games. Participants also had the opportunity to experience electric mobility, including rides on electric buses and electric bicycles. According to Mr Omaboe, the initiative was intended to demonstrate the possibilities of transforming urban streets into inclusive public spaces where people can engage in activities beyond commuting. “The idea is to close the street and give people the opportunity to use the street to do any activity that they want beyond moving by vehicular transport,” he explained. He said the fair had generated considerable curiosity among residents, particularly because streets are more commonly closed for funerals and other traditional activities rather than recreational and community-centred engagements. Mr Omaboe, however, identified the excitement among children as one of the most encouraging aspects of the event. He observed that many children enthusiastically participated in the painting and recreational activities, describing the opportunity as particularly important at a time when children have limited spaces to freely engage in such activities within their communities. “What we’ve seen is a lot of kids really excited about how they are using the street today. Children these days don’t have the chance to do that freely in the communities that they are in, and I think it’s one of the highlights of the Open Street Fair,” he said. He believes the experience should encourage city authorities and urban planners to reconsider the allocation of road space and invest in infrastructure that accommodates different categories of road users. Mr Omaboe stressed that the distinction between road infrastructure and car infrastructure was important in changing public attitudes towards urban mobility. “There’s a reason why we say road infrastructure and not car infrastructure. Streets do not only belong to cars,” he said. He advocated the development of dedicated cycling infrastructure and pedestrian lanes to make streets safer and more accessible to people who choose to walk or cycle. He added that the broader vision was to promote urban environments that integrate art, mobility, recreation and social interaction while strengthening connections within communities. The Open Street Fair forms part of efforts by Transform Transport Accra to demonstrate how public spaces can be reimagined to prioritise people, encourage sustainable mobility and create more inclusive urban communities.

items.title: Sandpapergate controversy deepens as ex-Australia bowler Chadd Sayers also claims ‘everyone knew’
items.description: Former Australian Test bowler Chadd Sayers backed Usman Khawaja over his “ Sandpapergate ” claims on Sunday, contradicting Pat Cummins’ denials that he knew nothing about the ball-tampering plot. Sayers was on the tour of South Africa but did not play in the third Test at Cape Town in 2018, where sandpaper was used to help make the ball swing. A Cricket Australia (CA) probe concluded only then-skipper Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were in the know, with all sent home and banned. But Khawaja alleged in his autobiography last week that the whole team was aware , a claim strongly backed by Warner and now Sayers. “I believe that everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used,” the retired Sayers, who played in the fourth Test at Johannesburg, told SEN radio. Khawaja also alleged sandpaper was used in the second Test at Port Elizabeth, with Sayers saying he was the one who took it from the field. “It (sandpaper) was given to me to take off, so that wasn’t planned or anything. I was just the player who took the drinks out at the time,” he said. “It was used in two Test matches and there was discussions in the change rooms of how we were going to get the ball to reverse and what was going to be used.” Cummins, now the Test captain, held a lengthy press conference on Friday to rubbish Khawaja’s allegations, calling them “100 per cent wrong”. The bowling group of Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, Nathan Lyon and Cummins all denied publicly in a 2021 statement that they were aware of the plan. Cricket Australia have ruled out reopening their investigation. Warner on Saturday accused the governing body of “a cover-up”, saying that “as far as he knew” they did not interview Hazlewood, Starc or Lyon at the time. “If that’s correct then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn’t know?,” he said. After numerous media reports confirmed the bowlers had indeed been interviewed, Warner on Sunday posted another statement on Instagram. “Just to clarify ‘As far as I am aware’ was the POINT,” he wrote. “I was never told the bowlers had been interviewed or provided statements. That information would’ve been pretty useful when I was forced to make decisions back in 2018. “Why weren’t we given all the evidence by CA?” View this post on Instagram

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : 104 élèves-athlètes bénéficient d’un accompagnement scolaire spécialisé
items.description: Au lendemain des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026, le ministère de l’Éducation nationale entend éviter que l’engagement sportif des jeunes athlètes ne se fasse au détriment de leur parcours scolaire. À cet effet, Moustapha Mamba Guirassy a annoncé un dispositif d’accompagnement pédagogique destiné à 104 élèves-athlètes , comprenant notamment la remise d’ordinateurs, la désignation de professeurs référents et des programmes personnalisés de rattrapage. Les exploits sportifs ne doivent pas se transformer en retard scolaire. C’est le message porté par le ministre de l’Éducation nationale, Moustapha Mamba Guirassy, lors d’une rencontre avec les élèves-athlètes sénégalais au Village olympique. Au lendemain de leur participation aux JOJ Dakar 2026, ces jeunes sportifs bénéficient d’une attention particulière des autorités éducatives, soucieuses de préserver la continuité de leur apprentissage. Au total, 104 élèves-athlètes sont concernés par ce dispositif d’accompagnement spécialisé. L’objectif est de leur permettre de concilier les exigences de la pratique sportive de haut niveau avec celles de leur scolarité. Pour le ministère, aucun jeune ne devrait avoir à choisir entre sa passion pour le sport et la poursuite de ses études. Cette démarche repose sur un accompagnement pédagogique adapté aux contraintes des jeunes sportifs. Elle prévoit notamment la remise d’ordinateurs portables, la désignation de professeurs référents ainsi que l’élaboration de plans personnalisés de rattrapage scolaire. Ces mesures seront également soutenues par les plateformes numériques éducatives du ministère. Au-delà de la reconnaissance des performances réalisées sur les terrains, cette initiative traduit une volonté de faire du sport un levier de réussite et d’épanouissement pour la jeunesse. Les valeurs de discipline, de persévérance, d’effort et de dépassement de soi, mobilisées dans les compétitions, peuvent également contribuer à la réussite scolaire. À travers ce dispositif, le ministère entend ainsi inscrire l'héritage des JOJ dans la durée. Car si les jeunes athlètes ont défendu les couleurs nationales sur les terrains, leur avenir se construit aussi sur les bancs de l’école. A.N

items.title: Fiat Algérie lance une nouvelle version du Doblo Panorama dès 3,869 millions DA
items.description: En attendant la Grande Panda qui tarde à sortir de son usine à Oran, Fiat Algérie lance une nouvelle version du Doblò Panorama à partir de 3,869 millions de dinars. L’annonce a été faite par Fiat El Djazaïr ce dimanche 15 novembre. Doblò Panorama Street est une édition limitée produite à l’usine de Tafraoui « destinée aux familles algériennes », indique Fiat El Djazaïr . Ce nouveau modèle se distingue par une « identité stylistique audacieuse et des équipements dédiés au confort, à la technologie embarquée et à la sécurité », ajoute la même source. « Cette version vient enrichir ponctuellement la gamme du Fiat Doblò Panorama, aux côtés des versions Cult et Club qui sont toujours proposées aux clients », précise encore Fiat Algérie. Le Fiat Doblò Panorama Street destiné aux clients déjà inscrits pour le Doblò Panorama Le Fiat Doblò Panorama Street se distingue par sa teinte « Cinema Black », un spoiler arrière, un badge « Street » apposé sur le hayon, des jantes en alliage de 16 ou 17 pouces, un combiné d’instrumentation numérique de 10 pouces, un écran tactile FIAT TOUCH Plus Full HD de 10 pouces, une caméra de recul et un radar de stationnement arrière. « Les poignées de porte noir brillant « Gloss Black », les rails de portes et le pare-chocs arrière noirs complètent sa signature extérieure, au même titre que les barres de toit et les vitres arrière surteintées. Il bénéficie également de projecteurs FIAT EcoLED, d’antibrouillards avant et de la Magic Window », détaille Fiat El Djazaïr. Le Doblò Panorama Street est doté « d’airbags frontaux et latéraux, d’un système de surveillance de la pression des pneumatiques (TPMS), du verrouillage centralisé, d’une roue de secours et d’une protection en tôle sous le moteur, qui font également partie de la dotation. » Fiat Algérie précise que cette nouvelle version s’adresse aux « clients déjà inscrits pour le Doblò Panorama », en ajoutant que les inscriptions sont traitées par « ordre chronologique ». Pour ceux qui sont déjà inscrits, leur distributeur agréé FIAT les « contactera pour leur proposer, selon les disponibilités, un Doblò Panorama Cult ou Club, ou l’édition limitée Street ». items.title: South Korea probes top exam scorer after AI cheating confession
items.description: South Korean police said Sunday they had launched an investigation after the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam admitted to using artificial intelligence to cheat. The candidate, who ranked first in both rounds of the qualification exam held in April and July, confessed through his lawyer that he used AI to obtain answers during the tests. His score of 397.5 out of 400 points in the first round, with only one wrong answer out of 160 questions, had sparked accusations that he cheated using smart glasses , which he initially denied. “We received a written confession through the test taker’s lawyer this morning regarding cheating on the tax accountant exam,” the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said, adding the case had been assigned to investigators. In a video posted on his lawyer’s YouTube channel, the candidate said he “deeply regretted” what he had done. “I used a miniature camera to photograph the exam questions and sent them to AI, then checked the answers on my smartphone,” he said. The individual said he had struggled financially after leaving his job to start a business. “I wanted to make money, and I hated seeing myself disappointing my parents after quitting a good job,” he said. His lawyer said further details would not be disclosed over concerns other cheaters could copy the method. The examination is administered by the Human Resources Development Service of Korea (HRDK), which said two supervisors were present when the candidate sat the test. HRDK president Lee Byung-hoon apologised for the incident and said the agency would file a criminal complaint against the test-taker for obstruction of business. With the highly competitive annual college entrance test, known as the “Suneung”, due to take place on November 19, the presidential office said it was treating the issue seriously. At a meeting held Sunday, officials decided to comprehensively investigate all suspected cases of cheating involving AI across national qualification examinations, according to the presidential office. Authorities have recently stepped up efforts against cheating involving smart glasses. The HRDK said Sunday an “AI inspector” caught a test taker wearing smart glasses during a gas engineer certification exam last month. In October, the government announced plans to file criminal complaints against students caught using such devices in the national university entrance exam.

items.title: Bono East NDC: Incumbent chairman ousted as Alhaji Ali Abubakar secures victory
items.description: Chief Executive Officer of Akina Group of Companies, Alhaji Ali Abubakar, popularly known as “Soldierman,” has defeated incumbent Unas Owusu to become the new Bono East Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC). Mr Abubakar polled 155 votes against Mr Owusu’s 118 in the regional executive elections held at the Nkoranza Technical Institute on Saturday. The polls, which ended at 4:00 p.m., were followed by the sorting and counting of ballots. The result ends Mr Owusu’s tenure as regional chairman, a position he had held since the creation of the Bono East Region. Regional Electoral Commission officer Dr Gabriel Dei Yeboah announced the results and congratulated the successful candidates. He also commended delegates for their conduct during the exercise. “I congratulate the new chairman and all the elected executives,” he said. “The process was transparent, and I commend the delegates for their peaceful conduct throughout the exercise.” The elections also resulted in changes to several other positions on the regional executive, with a number of incumbents losing their bids for re-election, including the Regional Women’s Organizer. New executives were elected for the positions of Regional Secretary, Deputy Secretary, First and Second Vice Chairmen, Treasurer, Deputy Treasurer, Women’s Organizer and Deputy Youth Organizer. The Zongo Caucus Coordinator and Deputy Regional Communications Officer positions were uncontested. In his acceptance speech, Mr Abubakar thanked the Electoral Commission, the Ghana Police Service, the media and other stakeholders for their roles in ensuring the peaceful conduct of the elections. He pledged to work with all members of the party, including candidates who lost, to strengthen the NDC in the region. “I will work with all, including those who lost, to ensure we work together for the success of the party,” he said. A total of 398 delegates voted in the elections, which were conducted under security provided by more than 400 police personnel. Voting was delayed by the late arrival of some delegates but proceeded peacefully, with no incidents reported during the counting of ballots.

items.title: Daffiama-Bussie-Issa set for major STEM school as Jakpa, DCE inspect project
items.description: Director of Operations at the National Security Secretariat, Richard Jakpa, together with the District Chief Executive (DCE) for Daffiama-Bussie-Issa, James Wor, has inspected construction works on a major STEM school project in the district. The project has been described as the single most important and biggest investment in Daffiama-Bussie-Issa (DBI) since its creation. Funded by the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund), the project was lobbied for the district by Mr Jakpa. The sprawling campus will feature a three-storey, 18-unit classroom block, a two-storey science laboratory, a two-storey library and ICT hub, and a two-storey administration block. After touring the site with the contractor, Mr Jakpa said he was impressed with the pace and quality of work. “We took a walk with the contractor, and so far, from the time I cut the sod for the commencement of the project to today, I’ve seen very fast progress. He has done so much. He has done well, and I’m very impressed with the quality of the work. You can really see the quality of the columns, the concrete, everything, and I’m very, very impressed,” he said. Mr Jakpa expressed optimism that the project would be completed on schedule, with commissioning expected by the end of June next year. “I’m hoping that we’ll be able to meet the deadline so that by the middle of next year, by the end of June, God willing, we should be preparing to come and commission the school. His Excellency will be here, God willing, to commission the first STEM SHS in the northern part of the country,” he said. He said the school would provide young Junior High School (JHS) graduates with the opportunity to pursue science and technology education and develop into engineers and science-oriented graduates capable of contributing to national development. According to him, Ghana needs to place greater emphasis on science education rather than continue producing graduates whose training is predominantly in the humanities. “We’ll have a lot of graduates in this country, but a lot of them are humanities-oriented graduates. We need to start focusing more on science graduates to be able to propel this country to the next level,” he said. Mr Jakpa said science and technology were essential to developing local manufacturing and providing practical solutions to challenges facing the agricultural sector. “It’s science that can help us manufacture basic things for the agro-industry, so that our farmers, because we are in an agrarian economy, should be able to access basic equipment and products to reduce post-harvest losses,” he added. Beyond the Daffiama-Bussie-Issa project, Mr Jakpa is advocating a nationwide initiative to establish 10 STEM senior high schools in 10 districts every year until every district in Ghana has one. He said the initiative could be implemented gradually as a long-term national development project. “If we are able to build one STEM SHS in all the districts in the country as an objective of government, it won’t happen in one day, but we can build 10 at a time. Every year, we award contracts for 10. In the next 20 years or so, we should have all our districts with one STEM SHS each. It can be a 20-year project,” he said. For his part, the DCE for Daffiama-Bussie-Issa, James Wor, commended the contractor for the quality of work and said he was satisfied with the progress made so far. He used the inspection to respond to claims on social media suggesting that little or no work was taking place at the project site. “My heart is most impressed by the quality of work. You see the materials on site, you see the work they are doing; it is top-notch, and I’m highly impressed,” he said. Mr Wor urged those spreading what he described as false information about the project to desist, insisting that the level of work on site was evident. “I want to use this forum to plead with and urge those who want to send DBI backwards by spreading false propaganda to stop. I’ve seen on social media where people indicate that there is nothing happening on site. We are all here. You, the media people, are here with your cameras, and you can see the level of work,” he added. He described the school as the biggest and most important investment in the district since its creation and appealed to residents to support the project and the contractor. “This is a laudable project. It’s a very important project. I call it the single most important and biggest investment we have in DBI at the moment since its creation. And so, let’s all support it. Let’s support the contractor,” he said. The DCE also praised the contractor for what he described as his commitment to corporate social responsibility, including plans to renovate the police quarters in Issa, support the local health facility and engage local artisans in the construction work. He said the contractor had provided opportunities for artisans within the district to contribute to the project while receiving training and payment for their work. “He has taken certain things up as part of his social responsibility. For instance, he’s indicated that he will renovate our police quarters for us in Issa. He is also making good use of our local artisans. Many of the people you see working here are artisans within the district whom his technical team is training, and that is good. They are also being paid,” Mr Wor said. He urged residents to have confidence in local workers, saying their contribution to the project demonstrated their ability to deliver quality work. “We shouldn’t underrate our own people. You look at these quarters being done, look at the quality. They are workers from DBI whom I recommended to him, and he took them on. They are doing a good job,” he added. The Managing Director of TMJ Ghana Limited, the contractor undertaking the project, Jonah Johafoka, said the school was particularly important to his company because of its commitment to bringing high construction standards to the Upper West Region. He said although the contract was awarded through GETFund, the company had a personal interest in ensuring that the project met high standards, given its roots in the region. “This contract, as you all know, is from GETFund, but personally, it’s so dear to us, not just because it’s the first STEM school here, but because we, as contractors, have been based in Accra and want to bring Accra’s standards to the Upper West Region, where we come from,” he said. Mr Johafoka identified heavy rainfall as the main challenge affecting construction, explaining that the weather had made it difficult to transport materials and equipment to the site. He said some construction equipment had become stuck in the mud during the rainy season, delaying work, but conditions had since improved. “We’ve not had many challenges except the weather. We had severe rains, and bringing materials to the site, as you see today, was not possible a month ago because of the rain. We had our dozers fall down here. We had a tipper stuck here for weeks before we were able to pull it out. So, the rains disturbed us, but now we’ve picked up, and we hope to move forward,” he said. The contractor disclosed that the project was approximately 25 per cent complete, with the foundation stage, which he described as the most critical part of the construction, completed. “We are around 25 per cent complete because the foundation is the most critical stage, and we are through with that. As you can see, the columns are coming up. In a week’s time, we should be working on the columns and decking,” he added. On payments, Mr Johafoka said he did not anticipate any major difficulties and was expected to submit the company’s first payment certificate within a week. Mr Wor concluded by expressing gratitude to President John Dramani Mahama, GETFund, Mr Jakpa for lobbying for the project, and the contractor for the work done so far. When completed, the school is expected to expand access to science, technology, engineering and mathematics education in Daffiama-Bussie-Issa and the wider northern part of the country, while helping to develop the critical thinkers, engineers and innovators needed to support Ghana’s development.
