items.title: Peshawar ATC moves to declare Sohail Afridi proclaimed offender in Radio Pakistan attack case
items.description: PESHAWAR: An anti-terrorism court here has started proceedings to declare dysfunctional Chief Minister Sohail Afridi as a proclaimed offender in the Radio Pakistan attack case as the relevant police official claimed that Mr Afridi couldn’t be traced. In the order sheet, Judge Wali Mohammad Khan noted that the detective foot constable (DFC) of the East Cantonment police station returned the warrants issued against the accused, including Sohail Afridi and Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf activist Mohammad Amir Khan, with overleaf reports stating that both of them couldn’t be found or traced. “Proclamation notices under Section 87 of CrPC should be issued against accused Sohail Afridi and Amir Khan, with notice to the DFC for recording a corroborative statement,” he said. He fixed Nov 24 for submission of the DFC’s report and further proceedings. Police official says dysfunctional CM remains untraced The judge had ordered the issuance of arrest warrants for the accused on Oct 28 after a supplementary charge-sheet was submitted, naming Afridi, Amir, former provincial ministers Taimoor Saleem Khan and Kamran Bangash and PTI Peshawar president Irfan Saleem as the accused in the May 2023 ransacking and torching of the Radio Pakistan building in Peshawar. Subsequently, the court issued warrants against Afridi and Amir on Nov 5. The warrants issued for Mr Afridi’s arrest listed his residential address in Bara, Khyber district. However, they didn’t describe Mr Afridi as the dysfunctional chief minister. The other three newly nominated accused appeared before the court and were granted interim pre-arrest bail. The dysfunctional chief minister has not been seen since the imposition of the governor’s rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Oct 11. While his whereabouts remained unknown, first a federal minister and then some other government functionaries disclosed that he and some of his cabinet members were in preventive custody. The other accused, Amir Khan, was also reportedly taken into custody a few days ago but has so far not been produced before any court. The alleged illegal detention or abduction of Mr Afridi was challenged by his brother, Amir Khan, in the Peshawar High Court. However, the court halted proceedings in the matter after the Federal Constitutional Court suspended its powers to hear cases under Article 199 of the Constitution. Section 87 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) states: “If any Court is satisfied after taking evidence that any person against whom a warrant has been issued by it has absconded or is concealing himself so that such warrant cannot be executed, such Court may publish a written proclamation requiring him to appear at a specified place and at a specified time not less than thirty days from the date of publishing such proclamation.” The law also provides that a proclamation issued by the court shall be publicly read in some conspicuous place of the town or village in which such person ordinarily resides; it shall be affixed to some conspicuous part of the house or homestead in which such person ordinarily resides or to some conspicuous place of such town or village. A copy must also be affixed to a conspicuous part of the courthouse. Last month, the prosecution submitted a supplementary charge-sheet, nominating Mr Afridi and the other four PTI members as accused in the case. None of them had been named in the first information report or earlier charge-sheet. The supplementary charge-sheet followed findings by the Punjab Forensic Science Agency and the National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra) regarding video clips purportedly showing the incident and profile pictures of the suspects. According to a report by investigation officer Deputy Superintendent of Police Khushal Khan, Radio Pakistan Peshawar station director Tufail Ahmad recorded a supplementary statement in light of the forensic findings, nominating the five men as accused. The forensic examination was ordered on Dec 12, 2025, on an application filed by the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation’s counsel, Shabbir Hussain Gigyani. The PFSA subsequently concluded that the facial features of the five men matched those of suspects allegedly seen participating in the rioting in the video footage. A Nadra report identified CNIC numbers apparently belonging to the men and described them as probable matches for the profile pictures submitted for examination. The newly nominated accused have challenged the authenticity of the videos, claiming that the footage doesn’t relate to the incident. The court is currently conducting the trial of 75 accused in the case, including current and former lawmakers. The FIR was registered at the East Cantonment police station on May 10, 2023, on the complaint of then station house officer Arbab Naeem Haider under various provisions of the Pakistan Penal Code and the Anti-Terrorism Act. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: “Os deseo sufrimiento”: gloria y caída de Jensen Huang, rey de Nvidia, verso salvaje de la IA
items.description: Jensen Huang es el protagonista de una historia imposible , una de esas epopeyas de superación y gloria que han ayudado a cimentar el mito estadounidense de las oportunidades, de país joven, rico y salvaje donde todo es posible con esfuerzo. Nacido en Taiwán en 1963, llegó a los nueve años a Estados Unidos junto a su hermano, como menor no acompañado, con el fin de reunirse con un tío que vivía en el Estado de Washington, pero que lo internó por error en una academia para chicos problemáticos en Kentucky. Los padres lograron emigrar a los dos años y la familia se reunió en Oregón, donde Jensen destacó en los estudios y logró su primer empleo sirviendo mesas en la cadena de comida rápida Denny’s. Se graduó en ingeniería eléctrica dos años antes de lo habitual. En la universidad conoció a Lori Mills, una de las pocas chicas que estudiaban esa carrera, y se casaron. Seguir leyendo

items.description: Cuando Laura Marchena pidió un préstamo al banco, nunca imaginó que tendría que pasar los siguientes 12 años pagando por 26.000 euros de los que nunca llegó a disponer. Lo que no sabía es que el supuesto empleado que, creía, la estaba ayudando a evitar un fraude, en realidad le iba a vaciar la cuenta. “Se presentó con sus credenciales y me dijo que un señor de Albacete estaba intentando pedir un préstamo a mi nombre. Para bloquearlo tenía que pedirlo yo primero y luego devolverlo al banco”, relata esta mujer, que prefiere utilizar un nombre ficticio para contar su historia. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Política y finanzas juegan a favor de Hernández de Cos para la presidencia del BCE
items.description: La carrera por presidir el Banco Central Europeo parece un sprint, pero aún no ha terminado, y se acerca más a una maratón, por más que los acontecimientos se hayan sucedido a velocidad de vértigo. El pasado 29 de octubre, la presidenta Christine Lagarde anunciaba su dimisión, efectiva el 7 de febrero. Este viernes, dos semanas después, el canciller alemán Friedrich Merz anunciaba que el acuerdo final es cuestión de días . A fecha de hoy, el favorito cada vez más claro es el español Pablo Hernández de Cos, director gerente del Banco Internacional de Pagos de Basilea y exgobernador del Banco de España, por delante del otro candidato oficial, el holandés Klaas Knot. Aunque, como advertía el líder alemán en Dublín este mismo viernes: “Las conversaciones tampoco han concluido todavía”. Y eso quiere decir que, en el poco tiempo que falta para adoptar la decisión, el escenario puede cambiar. Seguir leyendo

Últimamente le parecen más frecuentes y las explosiones se sienten más cerca. La casa, los cristales y hasta la luz, tiemblan. Ante el temor a que los ataques rusos alcancen suelo polaco, especialmente en las regiones fronterizas de Podkarpackie y Lubelskie , las autoridades han reactivado las sirenas antiaéreas, calladas desde la II Guerra Mundial. “No puedo decir que no tenga miedo, pero prefiero no pensarlo mucho”, dice Barbara (no da el apellido) antes de entrar en el supermercado. items.title: ¿Qué es El Niño? Así enloquece el clima global una pequeña región tropical del Pacífico
items.description: Imagine una olla puesta al fuego con el agua bullendo hasta el borde. Añada un cazo más y el líquido hirviendo acabará rebosando. Es lo que está ocurriendo con el fenómeno de El Niño , un evento natural y cíclico que trastoca el clima en muchas partes de la Tierra, eleva la temperatura media mundial, acarrea pérdidas milmillonarias, hambrunas, muertes... El Niño es ese cazo último que se vierte sobre un planeta sobrecalentado ya por el cambio climático causado por el ser humano, principalmente, con el uso de los combustibles fósiles durante demasiadas décadas a pesar de las alertas científicas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Emma Suárez: “Me he quitado la ansiedad de llegar a todo y a todos. Ahora me toca a mí”
items.description: La veo desde lejos, inconfundible con su aire casual y su eterno flequillo rubio, sentada en un velador como única clienta de un elegante y acristalado quiosco madrileño en una mañana gris y lluviosa, componiendo una estampa a lo musa de Hopper , si Hopper hubiera sido madrileño y no gringo y Madrid tuviera mar y no río. Fuera, el otoño explota en toda la gama del rojo al ocre en los espectaculares árboles del Parque del Oeste, aumentando la sensación de oasis de calma entre las prisas urbanas de un martes víspera de una huelga general y del inicio de la campaña electoral. Se agradece. Vengo de ver Hermanas , la película en la que Emma Suárez interpreta a una esposa, madre, hermana y tía en un marco de abusos sexuales dentro de la familia, y tengo el corazón en un puño. Seguir leyendo UNA VIDA EN 110 PELÍCULAS Tenía 14 años cuando se presentó a unas pruebas, por probar, y resultó elegida. Era el casting de Memorias de Leticia Valle , la película basada en la obra de Rosa Chacel, y supuso el estreno en el cine, y en la actuación, de Emma Suárez (Madrid, 62 años). Desde entonces, ha participado en 110 películas, por las que ha ganado tres premios Goya, y decenas de obras de teatro y series de televisión. El 27 de noviembre estrena la película Hermanas , junto a Elena Anaya.

items.title: Será la edad
items.description: Sé que no suena ortodoxo en estos momentos, pero servidora, para acabar perpetrando esa celebración de la democracia que es el voto, ha decidido ahorrarse la campaña . Paradojas de la vida: un acto de responsabilidad alimentado por otro que, para algunos, sería de irresponsabilidad. En el cuento Justo el Treintaiuno, el uruguayo Onetti describe cómo una mujer se sienta a diario en el inodoro y lee un cartel que reza: “Gracias, Dios mío, por no haberme hecho mujer ni negro ni judío ni perro ni petizo”. Ironías onettianas aparte, yo diría, “Gracias, Dios mío, por no haberme hecho periodista política ni analista ni politóloga ni presentadora de informativos”, gracias, Señor, por hacerme tan carente de responsabilidades como para permitir que me ahorre algo que me hace sentir que mi reino no es de este mundo. No es que no me concierna lo que nos viene ocurriendo, en lo absoluto, pero el ruido me distrae. Con ruido no veo, como diría el enfermizo Juan Ramón. Tanta es mi confusión que cuando el jueves escuché en el desayuno que había comenzado la campaña pensé si no estaría perdiendo capacidad cognitiva, dado que yo pensaba que esto era algo que había comenzado hacía meses, qué digo meses, años, que vivíamos en campaña permanente, con esas homilías de los domingos que los informativos glosan o esas exabruptos que a diario nos avergüenzan. Ocurre que, de vez en cuando, la realidad nos saca del bucle, ocurre, por ejemplo, que un sindicato nacido de las puras necesidades sociales, el de inquilinas, consigue movilizar a partidos e incluso urge a las grandes organizaciones sindicales a hablar de lo que importa. Ocurre que por unos días la conversación se despereza, y se diría que lo que realmente importa vuelve a tomar la calle y a protagonizar las tertulias, pero ay, amigas, el baño de realidad acaba porque raudos nuestros clásicos se apoderan del asunto. Para la oposición, tanto huelguistas como manifestantes están manipulados por el diabólico Sánchez, de tal forma que cualquier protesta se califica de acto electoral, así catalogan las movilizaciones por la vivienda, la enseñanza, la universidad, los servicios públicos, la sanidad. El insulto es su manera de evitarse el mostrar un proyecto alternativo. Y es curioso porque esta permanente teoría acusatoria contra el Sánchez maniobrero acaba por librar al propio Sánchez de su parte de responsabilidad, que también la tiene. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Broncano y las inquilinas
items.description: Dos noticias, una misma historia. Un presentador de televisión se disculpa por decepcionar a su público y una huelga por la vivienda necesita recurrir a los sindicatos de clase para poder ser convocada. Dos episodios que, si se leen juntos, plantean una misma pregunta: ¿Qué ocurre con nuestros intermediarios, las instituciones que durante el siglo pasado organizaron nuestra manera de estar juntos en política? Al margen de reconocer su incomprensible entrevista a Abascal, de dejarse vampirizar por los intereses partidistas o aceptar que Vox pusiera sus propios espectadores, errores que él mismo reconoció, lo más revelador de Broncano fue decir que entre el programa y sus seguidores se ha generado una comunidad de “identificación”. El cómico hablaba de una relación que va más allá del entretenimiento, de una forma de pertenencia y confianza donde hay incluso cierta expectativa de representación; un público que se reconoce en él porque comparte una manera de mirar la realidad y espera que sea consecuente con ella. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El deseo de una lectora: “Ojalá alguien anónimo se subiera cada mes a la tribuna del Congreso a sacarles los colores”
items.description: Independientemente de los resultados de las votaciones del 29 de noviembre, pediría a las nuevas Cortes resultantes hacer un punto y aparte y dejar atrás el espectáculo vergonzante de enfrentamientos, insultos y gritos al que nos están sometiendo. Están allí para trabajar por y para todos nosotros y, desde la calle, créanme que no dan esa impresión. Es más, creo que se olvidan de lo que les ha llevado allí. Para recordárselo de vez en cuando y hacer que bajen a la tierra, pediría que, por lo menos una vez al mes, alguien anónimo, alguien de la calle, pudiera subir a ese estrado del Congreso, expusiera la realidad de la calle y les sacara a ustedes los colores. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Mélenchon se consolida en una Francia agitada
items.description: Doce del mediodía. Salón del Made in France en París. Quesos gigantes, embutidos, sartenes, navajas, café, vino. Producto nacional. El escenario perfecto para la foto electoral estos días. En una esquina, se mueve sin gracia, público ni magnetismo Éric Zemmour, candidato ultraderechista, xenófobo, supremacista. A pocos metros, decenas de personas, cámaras, muchísimos adolescentes de barrios populares ―sudaderas, plumones negros, deportivas― esperan a su ídolo como si fuera una estrella del trap . Entonces, un hombre de 75 años, blanco, canoso, bien vestido aparece por una puerta lateral. Lo opuesto a un ídolo de la generación Z. No es Zohran Mamdani, ni Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. No lleva coleta, no viste deportivas ni camisetas con eslóganes. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Israel asfixia la esperanza en Gaza tras más de un año de bloqueo a la reconstrucción
items.description: Mohammed Al Jalis estaba durmiendo con su mujer y su bebé de dos meses cuando le despertó el agua colándose en su tienda de campaña en Deir El Balah, donde ha acabado malviviendo, desplazado desde Al Tufah, un barrio del este de Ciudad de Gaza hoy mayoritariamente en manos —hasta nadie sabe cuándo— de las tropas israelíes. “Pensábamos que la lona y la esterilla impedirían que entrara, pero nos sorprendió ver que se inundaba por completo”, recuerda. El matrimonio salió de la tienda con el bebé “sin saber adónde ir” para encontrarse a más gente en la misma situación: con la ropa empapada en medio del frío y la lluvia. “No pudimos salvar nada. Casi todo se mojó: la comida, la harina, las mantas, los colchones...” Seguir leyendo

items.title: Sergio Ramírez: “Estos años de exilio han sido una lucha por aferrarme a mi lenguaje, por no perderlo”
items.description: Sergio Ramírez (Masatepe, Nicaragua, 84 años) es grande, sereno; camina ayudado de un bastón. Socarrón, dice que de su ingreso en la RAE, hoy a las 19.00, lo que le pone más nervioso es que tiene “que dar un paseo y subir a una grada, con el problema con la pierna”. Premio Cervantes en 2017 , luchador de la primera hora del sandinismo y exvicepresidente de Nicaragua, se exilió en España en 2021 y en 2023 el régimen de Ortega le despojó de su nacionalidad. Hoy dos detalles le señalan como heredero de Mario Vargas Llosa. El primero: ocupará su sillón, el L. El segundo: a él dedicará su discurso de investidura, Un novelista ecuménico . Se sienta. items.title: Middle power aspirations
items.description: AS the global order shifts away from unipolarity toward fragmented multipolarity, middle powers have gained unprecedented strategic weight. In a fragmented multipolar world, middle powers serve as indispensable diplomatic bridges and economic shock absorbers that keep the international system functioning despite great-power paralysis. Middle powers lack hegemonic ambitions, and retain the credibility to mediate active conflicts, build agile issue-specific coalitions, and maintain open trade and supply-chain corridors across rival blocs. Ultimately, these middle powers are preventing total global bifurcation of the international system between Washington and Beijing by stabilising their immediate regions and upholding international rules. However, scholars and policymakers rarely agree on a single checklist for middle power status, largely because different states exert influence through different mechanisms. Some, such as South Korea or Australia, earn the label through thriving, high-tech economies and global trade integration. Others, like Norway or Qatar, leverage niche diplomacy and active mediation to punch above their geographic weight. Still others, such as Türkiye and Pakistan, rely primarily on formidable military capabilities and regional security projection. Scholars generally evaluate middle power status across three core pillars including military capability, diplomatic outreach, and comprehensive national strength. National strength is largely defined by sustainable economic vitality and technological adaptation. Over the past two years, Pakistan has demonstrated a resurgence in the first two arenas, vaulting itself back into global strategic relevance. Yet, because its third and most foundational pillar remains weak, Pakistan’s recognition as an emerging middle power rests on a fragile foundation that cannot endure without a decisive domestic economic pivot. A credible middle power must possess the military capacity to defend its sovereignty and project stabilising influence across its neighbourhood. Between 2025 and 2026, Pakistan highlighted its hard-power credentials through both high-intensity deterrence and institutionalised defence partnerships . History shows that hard power and ingenious statecraft cannot substitute for domestic economic strength. During the brief but severe four-day conflict with India in May 2025, South Asia witnessed its first multi-domain confrontation integrating aerial clashes, drone swarms, and precision missile exchanges. Pakistan’s military response, culminating in Operation Bunyanum Marsoos, demonstrated modern warfare capabilities and aerial superiority. Pakistan’s swift military response compelled a rapid White House-facilitated ceasefire on May 10. By denying a larger neighbour unilateral escalation dominance, Islamabad reinforced its conventional and strategic deterrence. Since May 2025, Pakistan translated its battlefield credibility into a web of security pacts across the Middle East and the Muslim world. In September 2025, Islamabad and Riyadh signed the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement, and in August 2026, Pakistan joined Saudi Arabia and Türkiye to sign the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. These pacts not only created a formal collective deterrence network but also enhanced Islamabad’s strategic utility in the Gulf. The Badr agreement with Türkiye, Qatar, and Indonesia, has further strengthened Pakistan’s position as a net security provider of Arab Gulf states. Beyond military muscle, middle powers distinguish themselves through niche diplomacy. Following the outbreak of direct US-Israeli military hostilities against Iran in early 2026, traditional Gulf mediators found their channels strained. Adopting a posture of active neutrality, Islamabad stepped in. In March 2026, the US accepted Pakistan’s role as a primary conduit to Tehran, which led to the historic Islamabad peace talks in April 2026 and the subsequent June MoU that temporarily reopened the Strait of Hormuz. Even as the truce faced repeated strain through late 2026, the civil and military leadership of Pakistan continued shuttling proposals between Washington, Tehran, and European capitals. The decision to join Trump’s Gaza peace plan as a founding member also proved Islamabad could exercise diplomatic power beyond its immediate borders. However, despite these military and diplomatic milestones, history demonstrates that hard power and ingenious statecraft cannot substitute for domestic economic strength. In this third pillar, Pakistan exhibits severe structural deficits that undermine its middle power aspirations. Macroeconomic indicators showed surface stabilisation in FY2025-26 with inflation remaining between 7-9 per cent and GDP growth edging up to 3.7pc. However, the underlying growth model remains weak. For instance, investment hovers near 15pc of GDP, far below the 20-plus per cent threshold required to sustain the 6pc growth rates needed to absorb a booming youth population. Deindustrialisation and high energy costs continue to stifle export competitiveness. Foreign investors are largely concerned with the security situation in Balochistan and KP. Unrest in AJK has further marred prospects of foreign direct investment. The privatisation process is critically slow, while political consensus is absent over reforms for new provinces. With a low tax-to-GDP ratio and heavy external debt servicing, state solvency still relies heavily on remittances, multilateral bailouts, bilateral rollovers (such as a $3 billion Saudi cash deposit in April 2026) rather than productive capital formation. Hence, Pakistan today represents a textbook case of an asymmetric emerging middle power. Its disciplined military and seasoned diplomatic corps have successfully leveraged regional crises to earn Islamabad a seat at high-stakes global tables. However, geopolitical leverage built on security crises and external rent is inherently transactional. When regional wars subside or great-power priorities shift, Islamabad — lacking economic autonomy and technological innovation — will risk losing its strategic relevance. Therefore, to cement its status as a genuine middle power, Pakistan must execute an urgent domestic pivot. This requires dismantling elite economic capture, broadening the tax base, overhauling education to build a tech-literate workforce, and enhancing an export-driven industrial base. Until Islamabad matches its battlefield deterrence and diplomatic agility with sustainable economic sovereignty, its middle power status will remain an aspiration suspended over a precarious fault line. The writer is a strategic analyst of international security. The views expressed are his own. X: @itskhurramabbas Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Ligue des nations: Mbappé de retour face à la Turquie
items.description: L'attaquant Kylian Mbappé, forfait lors de la défaite des Bleus face à l'Italie jeudi (3-1), disputera la rencontre contre la Turquie dimanche à Bordeaux pour le compte de la Ligue des nations, a annoncé le sélectionneur Zinédine Zidane. « Mbappé sera avec nous demain », a affirmé Zidane devant les médias à la veille de ce match décisif pour la qualification en quarts de finale de la compétition. Touché aux ischio-jambiers mercredi à la veille du déplacement en Italie, le capitaine de l’équipe de France avait déclaré forfait avant de reprendre l'entraînement vendredi. Il était indisponible après le premier match de Zidane en tant qu’entraineur face à la Turquie (1-0), le 25 septembre, en raison d'une blessure au genou. Evoquant ses relations avec Mbappé, le sélectionneur a indiqué que « tout se passait parfaitement », relevant que la participation du meilleur buteur de l'histoire des Bleus dimanche « change tout ». Privés notamment de Kylian Mbappé et d'Ousmane Dembélé lors de la rencontre disputé à Milan, les Français se sont appuyés sur une attaque remaniée, avec Michael Olise, Désiré Doué et Bradley Barcola. Deuxième du groupe 1 à égalité avec l'Italie, la France aura besoin d’au moins un nul contre les Turcs pour valider son ticket en vue des quarts de finale de la Ligue des nations. The post Ligue des nations: Mbappé de retour face à la Turquie appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Judges must speak
items.description: A JUDGMENT is a public document, written in the name of the Constitution and delivered in open court. The people may read it, praise it and criticise it, and the academy, bar, press and civil society should do so freely. Criticism is not the enemy of judicial authority; it is its source. A judiciary whose judgments are never read critically will never grow. One voice is largely missing from that conversation: the judge who wrote the judgment. In Pakistan, judges mostly retire into silence. That must change. Retired judges must come out among the people, above all into the law schools, and explain their reasoning, or say, with hindsight: “I think I got that one wrong.” Such candour teaches the profession and builds public trust and confidence in the institution. A sitting judge who knows retirement means facing the public will brush nothing under the carpet. A judgment open to criticism falls into one of three kinds. The first plainly violates the Constitution and the law. The second was legally permissible when given, but its consequences proved damaging. The third is the judgment in which the judge was complicit, bending the law to reach an outcome decided elsewhere. To assess one, read it whole and in context: the moment, the circumstances, the law as it then stood. Then ask whether it was permissible, plainly wrong, or the judge simply listening to power. Let me test three of my own. In Pakistan, judges mostly retire into silence. That must change. In the 2023 case on Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa elections, Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail and I wanted the high courts to decide first: Lahore had already ordered elections, with appeals pending, and Peshawar was seized of the petitions. Law and practice both counselled that restraint. We read the outcome as four to three, because two colleagues who had already voted to dismiss could not, in our view, be dropped from the count; Justice Athar Minallah, one of them, recorded as much. In hindsight, the mistake, I believe, was the chief justice’s hurried leap in; hearing the matter in appeal, the court could have spoken with one voice. Had we set the count aside and presented a united court, whether that would have produced elections is anyone’s guess. Later, the chief justice’s own bench rejected the four-three objection and fixed May 14 for Punjab polls, yet could not enforce it. The date passed, contempt was never pursued, and the court fell silent. The larger lesson is that a court must stand united, and the chief justice’s strength is the real spine that holds it together. The Supreme Court as it stands today shows how much rests on that spine. In the Justice Qazi Faez Isa case , the court unanimously quashed the reference, the majority for malice in law; I held it malicious in fact as well. The majority directed the FBR to examine the family’s properties and report to the council; three of us held that no direction was needed, the FBR being free to act under the tax law. On review, that view prevailed. No one is above the law, and no one below its protection: a judge’s spouse answers under the tax law, a judge under the Code of Conduct, only in accordance with law. I am often asked whether we saved the wrong man. We saved due process and the independence of the judiciary, and in doing so we saved a man. What people thought of him later was not our concern then. A judgment is not a character certificate. In the Practice and Procedure case, I believed, and still believe, that the court had to become collegial rather than be run by one man. Opening the door was not itself the mistake; so long as the court stood united, no one could have walked through it. What we failed to see was that the court was weak within, and weakness inside invites those outside. And it did: a 2024 ordinance gave the chief justice’s nominee a seat on the bench-forming committee. Had earlier chief justices brought in the collegial model through the full court, that door need never have opened from outside. This is a lesson, not an accusation. Each choice was made in good faith, within the law. In hindsight, wiser choices may have been available, but choosing in the moment is the judicial function, and there the judge must be trusted. Unless a judge was complicit, there is nothing to apologise for, only lessons to share. What must worry us most is complicity. It is not an error of judgment but a surrender of it, and it has hollowed out our courts. A judgment bent to power may be overruled, but the betrayal stays on the record. Error is part of judging. Capitulation is not. And complicity has a way of showing its face, in the promotions, benefits and advantages that later reward it. Today, that trail must be made visible. A word to the critics. Those quick to call out judicial error must be as open-hearted in acknowledging courage. Dissent, refusal of oath and resignation are the building blocks of an independent judiciary. Ask what a judge gained by resigning when a simple yes would have secured everything. Nothing, except the honour of the institution. Criticism that records every failure and never that courage leaves the next generation no one to look up to. So let the conversation begin, and let it be honest. Let judges speak: give the context of their decisions, own their errors without fear and explain their choices without apology. And let complicity be named for what it is. Judicial independence has never been absolute. Sadly, there has always been a chink in the armour, a door left ajar, and someone willing to push it open. No single judgment or judge will close that door. But an honest and open conversation, carried from one generation to the next, can. That will be the real victory: not a court that never errs, but a court with no door through which power can enter. The writer is a professor of practice at SAHSOL, Lums, and currently a distinguished visiting fellow at Yale University. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Gas output halves in 10 years, says SSGC chief
items.description: KARACHI: The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) has been forced to restrict supply to domestic consumers three meal times a day because of depleting indigenous production over the past decade, its managing director said on Saturday. According to Muhammad Amin Rajput, the schedule was necessary as the country’s gas production had fallen about 50 per cent over the last decade, while imported LNG supplies, too, were hard to come by since April due to the Iran war. “By focusing on supply during cooking hours, the company can protect domestic consumers,” the managing director said in an exclusive interview with Dawn. He said SSGC’s gas availability had fallen to around 605 million cubic feet per day due to depletion in gas fields, compared with 695mmcfd last year. “Of this, around 300mmcfd is being given to domestic consumers, while the rest is supplied to industry, power and fertiliser sectors,” Mr Rajput added. The utility has decided to supply gas during the breakfast, lunch and dinner windows to ensure that every household got the fuel when it mattered most. “The SSGC has been monitoring availability continuously since last week,” Mr Rajput said. Supply to households restricted to three meal times He said domestic gas supply in the city was adequate. Residents in many areas, however, complained the flame was too low for cooking purposes. “A localised issue should not be generalised across the entire network that serves roughly 50,000 kilometres of pipelines, 16,000 of them in Karachi alone. The SSGC has 3.2 million customers across Sindh and Balochistan, including two million in Karachi,” Mr Rajput observed. Use of compressors, pumps The SSGC MD blamed the low pressure on the illegal use of gas compressors and suction pumps. These devices can drain away the supply to an entire block or building, he cautioned. “Besides being illegal, substandard devices pose safety risks and have caused property damage, and sometimes even loss of life.” Mr Rajput urged consumers to report such use, saying that removing the devices would help restore pressure during supply hours, even though they may inflate bills by distorting meter readings. He said his company had rehabilitated about 7,000 kilometres of distribution pipelines in 2025-26, replacing ageing and corroded pipes, mostly in Karachi. “That has improved pressure at tail-end locations and reduced unaccounted-for gas.” He said the situation was further compounded by substantially reduced availability of RLNG supplies from Qatar. “Besides meeting domestic requirements, the Petroleum Division has secured limited gas supplies to meet other critical needs. These include the power and fertiliser sectors,” the SSGC chief said. These competing requirements call for prudent management and judicious allocation of available resources. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Parliament’s nod deemed a must for referendum
items.description: • President, prime minister insist any move to create new provinces must follow Constitution • Zardari reiterates PPP’s opposition to division of Sindh • Naqvi’s ‘message’, Imran’s situation also discussed LAHORE: President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday agreed to “strictly adhere to constitutional provisions” governing the creation of new provinces or administrative units, with any proposed referendum on the contentious issue also requiring parliamentary approval. Official sources privy to the development told Dawn that the understanding was reached during a meeting between the two leaders at the prime minister’s Model Town residence, amid a fresh debate over the creation of additional provinces and a proposal by the interior minister to seek public opinion through a referendum. President Zardari, who was accompanied by former prime minister Raja Pervez Ashraf and Senator Saleem Mandviwalla, made it clear that the PPP’s position remained aligned with the Sindh Assembly’s resolution opposing the creation of new provinces. He stressed that any move in this direction must strictly follow the procedure prescribed by the Constitution, a position endorsed by PM Shehbaz, the sources said. PM’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq and the prime minister’s sons Hamza and Suleman were also present at the meeting. The two leaders also agreed that parliament could not be bypassed in deciding whether a referendum should be held and what questions should be put to the public, according to the sources. “The majority in parliament will decide whether a referendum is to be held and what its question(s) should be. Without consensus, the matter cannot move an inch. Parliament cannot be bypassed,” an official source quoted the meeting as agreeing. The discussion came two days after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi floated the idea of holding a referendum to gauge public opinion on the creation of new provinces or administrative units, arguing that the exercise could settle the debate once and for all. He had also assured political parties that they would be taken on board before any decision was finalised. However, the PPP leadership appears unwilling to soften its position, particularly on Sindh. The party has consistently invoked a unanimous resolution passed by the Sindh Assembly opposing the province’s division, maintaining that it reinforces its position against any such move. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and other senior party leaders have repeatedly declared that the division of Sindh is neither legally nor politically acceptable to the party. The debate has also highlighted differing positions within the ruling coalition. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif recently argued that Pakistan could have as many as 12 provinces if the exercise was guided by administrative requirements rather than linguistic, ethnic or political considerations. He maintained that the country’s growing population necessitated smaller administrative units capable of delivering public services more efficiently. However, the PML-N has so far refrained from articulating a formal policy, saying it would present its position when the matter came before parliament. Naqvi’s message, Imran’s issue The sources said President Zardari and PM Shehbaz also held a brief one-on-one meeting to discuss a message reportedly conveyed to the president by Interior Minister Naqvi during his recent visit to Nawabshah. The issue of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan also came under discussion. According to the sources, the meeting was informed that Mr Khan’s recent hours-long interaction with his lawyers and the release of his two sisters from jail were not linked to any particular behind-the-scenes deve­lopment. Meanwhile, a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office said the two leaders held detailed discussions on the country’s overall political, economic and security situation, emphasising coordination among the ruling coalition partners. The official statement did not specifically mention the discussion on new provinces or the proposed referendum. PM Shehbaz also briefed President Zardari on his recent visit to Turkiye, where he attended the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) and highlighted Pakistan’s efforts on climate action. The two leaders exchanged views on cooperation among allied parties, continued consultation and progress on public welfare initiatives. They reaffirmed their commitment to working together to accelerate economic stability and development, the statement added. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Creating new smaller provinces a ‘national necessity’: Kamal
items.description: KARACHI: Senior Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) leader and Federal Health Minister Syed Mustafa Kamal on Saturday called the creation of smaller provinces “a national necessity” and not a “political desire”, arguing that the existing four-province administrative structure has failed to deliver and that the formation of new provinces is essential for the effective functioning of the state. Addressing the inauguration ceremony of the Sindh regional office of the Allied Health Professionals Council (AHPC), the minister said Pakistan’s provinces were exceptionally large compared with those of many countries worldwide. He said Punjab alone had a larger population than 180 countries, while the other three provinces were also more populous than many countries. Referring to dozens of provinces Iran, Afghanistan and India have, he highlighted the difference between Pakistan’s administrative structure and those of other countries in the region. The minister said that 57.5 per cent of the divisible federal revenue pool was allocated to the provinces, which had received a combined Rs8,844 billion during the current financial year. However, he regretted that the funds were not reaching villages and grassroots communities because provinces had failed to devolve resources and authority further down the administrative hierarchy. MQM-P leader rejects concerns over national unity; likens new provinces to building additional rooms in a house to accommodate expanding family “The biggest problem is that the provinces have not devolved resources to the grassroots level. The money is being allocated to the provinces but unfortunately not reaching the villages,” he added. Describing Karachi as Pakistan’s economic engine, he said the city’s economic potential remained largely untapped, and it could play a pivotal role in pulling the country out of its economic difficulties. “Even 10pc of Karachi’s potential has not been tapped yet. The IMF cannot pull Pakistan out of this economic quagmire, but Karachi can,” he said. He explained that creating smaller provinces should not be seen as a threat to national unity. He gave an example of an expanding family that needed additional rooms to accommodate its growing members. “When a family grows, a new room has to be built. It does not mean that the house is being broken up or divided,” he said. Speaking about the AHPC’s regional office in Sindh, the minister called it an important step towards facilitating healthcare professionals and students in the province. He said they would no longer need to travel to Islamabad to resolve their professional and administrative issues. The new office would provide a one-window facility for allied health professionals, students and educational institutions across Sindh, enabling them to access information and seek solutions to their problems locally, he said, expressing the hope that similar council offices would be established in all provinces. The minister also stressed the need to transform Pakistan’s growing population into a skilled workforce, saying the government could not provide public-sector jobs to all 260 million citizens. He said creating employment opportunities for a rapidly expanding population remained a major national challenge and that the country needed to focus on skills development, technical education and human resource development. He said countries with large populations had achieved economic progress by investing in skills and developing their human capital, adding that Pakistan must adopt a similar approach, particularly for its youth. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: PMML serves legal notice on Maryam
items.description: LAHORE: The Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) on Saturday served a legal notice on Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, demanding that she withdraw her alleged remarks describing the party as a “terrorist, illegal and banned” organisation, and remove disputed content from social media and issue an unconditional public apology within seven days. Issued through a team of lawyers on behalf of PMML president Khalid Masood Sandhu, the notice accused Maryam Nawaz of making defamatory statements in a post on her X account and a public speech, which were subsequently aired repeatedly by television channels. The party warned that failure to meet its demands within seven days of receiving the notice would compel it to initiate appropriate legal proceedings before the competent courts, holding her responsible for all resulting costs and consequences. The legal move comes amid an escalating confrontation between the ruling PML-N and the PMML following the Nov 8 by-election in NA-77 Gujranwala. The PML-N retained the seat, with its candidate Rashid Bashir Virk securing 43,365 votes against 30,218 polled by PMML candidate Ibrahim Gujjar. The PMML rejected the outcome, claiming its candidate had actually won and demanded a recount in 50 polling stations. Maryam Nawaz and Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari subsequently questioned the PMML’s political credentials, alleging that proscribed organisations were operating under new names.The PMML maintains that it is a legally registered political party with the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) and has been functioning since 2022. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: The Lure of Fascist Fantasies
items.description: In the 1976 Hollywood classic Taxi Driver, Robert De Niro stars as a disturbed military veteran who works gruelling shifts as a cab driver through the decaying, sleazy backdrop of New York City. Plagued by chronic insomnia and living alone in a cramped apartment, he spends his nights ferrying passengers who seem to mirror the city’s moral collapse. He is a man of few words, and the film gradually lays bare his fragile state of mind through his internal monologues. In these voiceovers, he rails against the social ‘filth’ he encounters on the streets, culminating in a lament: ”All the animals come out at night… whores, buggers, queens, fairies, dopers, junkies, sick, venal. Someday a real rain will come and wash all this scum off the streets.” The lament can be interpreted as a fascist fantasy. Early in the film, the cabdriver attempts to court a campaign worker for a liberal presidential candidate, only to alienate her completely by taking her on a date to a pornographic cinema. Seemingly unable to comprehend why she is offended, he moves his obsession toward assassinating the candidate. The attempt fails. His focus then shifts to a young teenage sex worker. When he urges her to leave the trade, she asserts that she is entirely free to make her own choices. Undeterred, he returns later with lethal intent, launching a brutal armed assault that leaves her pimp and his associates dead. By the following morning, the media has reframed his violent spree as an act of ‘heroism’. In the chilling final scene, he is approached once more by the same woman who was once repulsed and offended by him, only this time she greets him with a smile. From Hollywood’s murderous anti-heroes to extrajudicial killings in Pakistan, ideological convictions and public frustration can make violence seem like an acceptable instrument of justice for both the left and right So, a disturbed man harbouring ‘fascist’ fantasies, who originally plotted to assassinate a politician, shifted his violent impulses. Eager to project his own idea of morality, he attempted to ‘rescue’ a young sex worker who had explicitly chosen her own path. His solution? Shoot her pimp and associates to death, thereby transforming himself into a ‘saviour’ and a ‘hero’, finally becoming the ‘rain’ he dreamed would wash the ‘scum’ off the streets. Director Martin Scorsese leaves the final moral judgment to the audience, framing an unsettling question: did the viewers feel a sense of satisfaction or outrage? How could a man evolve from a failed assassin into a murderous vigilante, only to be embraced as a media darling and societal hero? Nevertheless, one can suggest that the film is clearly conscious of the answer. Illustration by Abro Most viewers would justify the cabby’s actions. In troubled societies, where law and order is crumbling and whose moral compass seems to be going haywire, paranoia, anxiety and anger breed a dangerous appetite for vigilante action. When institutions fail and public safety feels like an illusion, audiences are dangerously primed to root for a violent reckoning. Therefore, an unstable, murderous anti-hero is perversely embraced because he steps in to do what an impotent system fails to do. So, what do you think is the actual reaction of most people when they read or hear about the extrajudicial killings of individuals accused of hideous crimes in Pakistan? Beneath the surface, there is often a quiet sense of satisfaction and, perhaps, even covert joy. Of course, ‘liberals’ are outraged, and rightly so, recognising that such actions and reactions are symptoms of a society teetering on the edge of a cliff, on the verge of tumbling straight into the lap of fascism. But those who have been crushed by the debris of a crumbling order are not the only ones who end up conjuring fascist fantasies or begin hailing actions that gradually nudge polities down fascism’s throat. This is not entirely a right-wing tendency, really. The embrace of fascism can come from the left and the liberals as well, especially when public frustration with the ‘system’ runs deep. A striking real-world echo of this phenomenon unfolded following the December 2024 murder of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in Manhattan. When the shooter was arrested, social media, and parts of the public, erupted in an unexpected wave of outright sympathy for him. Even individuals who would typically align with progressive or liberal values found themselves romanticising the murder of an ‘exploiter’. In January 2011, when the former Governor of Punjab, Salman Taseer, was gunned down by his police bodyguard for criticising Pakistan’s blasphemy laws, I was working at a European outlet operating in Karachi. At the office, I was rattled to witness a number of ‘liberals’ (both lifestyle and political), openly hailing the assassination. Some even went to extraordinary lengths to justify the murder, simply because they opposed Taseer’s political party. Troubled societies frequently create curious left-right trajectories and demonstrations of confused morality. These often converge on the same dangerous destination: a fascist order in the making, nourished by both the left and the right. In the 1995 film The Last Supper, five liberal graduate students accidentally kill a white racist and hatch a chilling plan: invite prominent right-wing figures to dinner, debate them and poison any guest who refuses to recant. They proceed to execute a rotating cast of bigots and extremists, burying them in their garden. The plot twists when they host a famous right-wing television talking head. Expecting a radical zealot, they are disarmed by his calm and rational demeanour and his admission that he does not actually believe his own rhetoric, but merely performs it for ratings. Confused, the students retreat to the kitchen to deliberate. They decide to spare him. Unbeknownst to them, though, the guest discovers their plot and switches the bottles of wine, one poisoned, one untainted. Thinking they are drinking untainted wine, the students start to die. The guest then casually lights a cigar. So who sympathised with whom? I’m sure liberal viewers saw the film as an anti-liberal farce. Yet, one can also posit that the anti-liberal lot weren’t overly enthused either, watching a right-winger confess he didn’t believe what he said on TV. In a way, he was making a fool of his core audience. The temptation of fascism wears many masks. It thrives whenever desperation or ideological zeal convinces us that the ends justify the means. Whether we cheer for the vigilante cab-driver, the assassin of a corporate executive, a mob that kills a supposed ‘blasphemer’, the unaccountable ‘justice’ provided to nasty people, or liberal students wielding poison in a suburban kitchen, we reveal a shared, perilous truth: when the rule of law breaks down, the applause for extrajudicial violence is the sound of a society eagerly digging its own grave. Published in Dawn, EOS, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Sales tax gets new enforcement structure to cut collection gap
items.description: ISLAMABAD: After 17 years of integration, the government has decided to reverse the functional integration of sales tax and income tax collection, acknowledging that the sales tax revenue gap has widened to Rs3.4 trillion amid weak enforcement and poor revenue collection. The decision marks a major reform in tax administration, providing for the selection of officers within the Inland Revenue Service (IRS) and the separation of functional responsibilities, including tax collection and legal matters, to address persistent weaknesses that have contributed to the revenue gap, senior tax officials told Dawn on Saturday. At the chief commissioner level, the administrative structure for sales tax and income tax will remain unchanged for now. However, functional separation will begin at the commissioner level and extend to subordinate officers, with dedicated officials assigned exclusively to sales tax matters. A dedicated member for sales tax and federal excise duty will report directly to the FBR chairman. The new member, with three chiefs and their teams, will give sales tax and federal excise duty continuous attention through data analysis, operations, and follow-up on selected cases. Government will separate sales and income tax functions within IRS Within each chief commissioner’s jurisdiction, separate sales tax zones will be established, headed by commissioners and supported by additional deputy and assistant commissioners. The restructuring will begin at Large Taxpayer Offices on Dec 1, followed by Corporate Tax Offices and Regional Tax Offices. The transition is expected to be completed within two months. The chief commissioners and Member IRS (Operations) will retain administrative and operational control, while the newly designated member will provide technical oversight and coordinate enforcement activities. Both taxes will continue to be administered within the IRS, rather than through separate services. As part of the process, the FBR has begun conducting specialised tests to identify officers with the required expertise in sales tax and income tax administration. “We have already launched an exercise to identify competent officers,” an official said, adding that the assessment would help assign officers to functions matching their professional capabilities. The need for functional separation also emerged from the widening sales tax revenue gap despite its relatively small taxpayer base. Sales tax accounts for nearly 55pc of the combined Rs6.2tr revenue gap, while approximately 90pc of its collections come from just 15,000 taxpayers, according to internal FBR estimates. Official figures showed that around 313,000 persons were registered for sales tax in early 2024, of whom only 190,000 filed tax returns, including many declaring no taxable transactions. In comparison, the number of active income tax return filers stood at approximately 6 million. It was pointed out that the integrated administrative structure had also weakened accountability, as IRS officers could meet their combined revenue targets by concentrating on income tax collections, while paying less attention to sales tax enforcement. A recent proficiency test conducted in Karachi further exposed the imbalance, with officers performing better in practical income tax matters than in sales tax administration, reflecting their greater exposure to income tax work. The FBR’s experience with production monitoring also demonstrated the benefits of targeted enforcement. In 12 manufacturing sectors where monitoring systems were introduced, the revenue gap declined by 12 percentage points of potential collections over two years, while it increased by nine percentage points in seven sectors without such systems. Under the new arrangement, specialised officers will analyse this information and pursue cases involving underreported sales, questionable input tax claims, and other compliance failures, rather than dividing their attention between income tax and sales tax responsibilities. In 2009, the then government, as part of the World Bank project, transferred the administration of sales tax and federal excise from Customs to the IRS. The major reasons for integration were that the two taxes are closely linked, because what an officer finds in a sales tax case often gives rise to an income tax demand, and that placing them under different officers would break this link. However, after 17 years of integration, official data showed substantial revenue gaps in both taxes, raising questions about the arrangement’s effectiveness. The sales tax revenue gap was estimated at Rs3.4tr, compared with Rs2tr for income tax. Officials said the original justification for integration had also weakened with the introduction of a common digital system operated by Pakistan Revenue Automation Ltd. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: World Bank okays $300m for Sindh’s water, sanitation services
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The World Bank has approved $300 million in financing to expand access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services for 1.5 million people in selected rural areas of Sindh. The financing will support the Sindh Trans­formational Accele­rated Rural Water Supply, Sanitation, and Hygiene Services Phase 1 Project (STAR WASH-1), the World Bank’s resident mission in Islamabad announced on Saturday. The project is expected to generate more than 14,000 jobs and support the formalisation of the Sindh People’s Housing for Flood Affectees as a rural water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) utility company. “Stunting is among Pakistan’s most severe and persistent human capital challenges, and unsafe water, sanitation and hygiene is a major underlying driver. By expanding access to these services for 1.5m people in rural Sindh, this project will help address one of the root causes of child stunting,” said Bolormaa Amgaabazar, the World Bank country director for Pakistan. Unsafe water and poor sanitation expose young children to repeated bouts of diarrhoea, impairing nutrient absorption and limiting their physical and cognitive development. More than half of children under five in rural Sindh are stunted. STAR WASH-1 aims to provide 1.5m people with access to safe drinking water and safely managed sanitation and hygiene services. The project will finance climate-resilient infrastructure, including solar-powered water supply systems and improved sanitation facilities. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan guidebooks author dies at 83
items.description: GENEVA: Isobel Shaw, an Irish-born travel writer whose guidebooks introduced thousands of visitors to Pakistan, died on Wednesday (Nov 11) at her home in St-Cergue, Switzerland. She was 83. Ms Shaw first came to Pakistan in 1978, when her husband, Robert Shaw, was posted to Islamabad as the Ford Foundation’s representative. During her three years in Islamabad she learnt Urdu and, with Hilary Adamson, wrote A Traveller’s Guide to Pakistan, published in Islamabad in 1981 and one of the first modern guidebooks to the country. Her Pakistan Handbook (1989) was shortlisted for the Thomas Cook Travel and Guide Book Awards, and her illustrated guide to Pakistan ran to five editions. With her son, Ben Shaw, she wrote the Pakistan Trekking Guide (1993) and a trekking guide to the Karakoram and Hindu Kush, published in Lahore in 2013. Other writers on the region recommended her as the best guidebook writer on Pakistan. During the 1990s she worked as a tourism consultant to the government of Pakistan and gave the keynote address at the Pakistan Tourism Convention in Karachi in 1993. After the 2005 earthquake she gave talks to raise funds for orthopaedic care for survivors. The same year, the Pakistan Society in London honoured her for advancing public knowledge and understanding of Pakistan in Britain. Her last book, Trekking Guide to the Karakoram and Hindu Kush of Northern Pakistan, was published by Vanguard Books in Lahore in 2013. She returned to Chitral that year, at the age of 70. Born Isobel O’Beirne in Meath, Ireland, in 1943, she studied at Newnham College, Cambridge. She had lived near Geneva since 1981 and is survived by her three children, nine grandchildren and a great-granddaughter. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Hamas says senior armed commander killed in Israeli strike
items.description: Hamas' armed wing said on Sunday that ​a senior commander who helped plan and oversee the ‌October 7, 2023, attack on Israel had been killed in an Israeli air strike. The Al-Qassam Brigades identified the commander as Samir Abu ​Younis, 53, the commander of its Rafah brigade, and ​said he was killed on Saturday. The Israeli military said on Sunday that it had struck a senior commander ​in Hamas' armed wing but did not identify him. Medics said ​Abu Younis was killed, and others were wounded in an air strike that targeted him in a street in the Mawasi area of ​Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip. Hamas said Abu ​Younis joined Hamas' armed wing in 1991 and had held several senior ‌operational roles in Rafah before becoming commander of the brigade. Hamas said his funeral would be held on Sunday afternoon in Khan Younis. An October 2025 ceasefire halted major fighting but has ​not stopped ​Israeli attacks or secured Hamas' disarmament. Gaza health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since ​the ceasefire went into effect. Five Israeli ​soldiers have been killed during the same period. Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel's military campaign against Gaza, ​launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about ​1,200 people in southern Israel in October 2023. items.title: Microsoft announces service 'restored,' global outage over
items.description: Tech giant Microsoft said on Saturday it had "restored service" to customers, effectively bringing to a close a massive outage that caused chaos and disrupted public services and businesses around the world. "We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions," the US-based company said in an X post. Microsoft had already reported a "broad recovery" for Outlook email and other services the day before, stating that the major disruption was due to a technical issue and " not related to cyber or AI/agents ." The outage swept the globe on Thursday, taking the company's products offline in at least 74 countries and territories across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa, according to the monitoring site Downdetector. Microsoft had attributed the disruption to "elevated load" on its infrastructure. It said the outage affected its Outlook email service, as well as its Teams communication platform and Copilot AI assistant. Microsoft warned on Saturday of an "active phishing campaign" exploiting the disruption, with fake emails imitating its service notifications. The emails, detected on Friday, told users that messages blocked during the outage would be deleted unless recipients clicked a link to restore them.

items.title: 86è session du Comité exécutif de l’UPA : Le président présente son rapport d’activités
items.description: Lomé, 14 nov. (ATOP) – Le président en exercice du Comité exécutif de l’Union parlementaire africaine (UPA) et président du Sénat de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), Jean-Michel Sama Lukonde Kyenge, a présenté, le samedi 14 novembre à Lomé, son rapport d’activités couvrant son mandat à la tête dudit comité. C’était au cours de la 86e session du Comité exécutif. Dans son rapport, le président a fait le point des actions menées depuis la 47e conférence de l’UPA, tenue à Kinshasa en novembre 2025. Il a notamment évoqué les initiatives diplomatiques engagées pour élargir et réactiver la participation des parlements membres, particulièrement en Afrique australe. En marge des assemblées de l’Union interparlementaire (UIP), des concertations bilatérales ont été menées avec l’Afrique du Sud, la Namibie, l’Angola et la Zambie. Ces démarches ont permis d’obtenir, à l’issue d’une mission à Lusaka le 29 octobre dernier, l’accord de principe des autorités parlementaires zambiennes pour le retour de leur institution au sein de l’UPA. Le Gabon a également été approché en vue de renforcer la participation des parlements nationaux sortant de périodes de transition. Abordant les questions financières, M. Sama Lukonde a invité les Etats membres à honorer régulièrement leurs cotisations et à apurer leurs arriérés. Il a salué le parlement marocain pour le règlement intégral de ses arriérés, d’un montant de plus de 370 000 euros. Sur le plan institutionnel, M. Sama a plaidé pour la finalisation de la révision des textes statutaires afin de permettre la création d’un caucus des jeunes, à l’image de celui des femmes. Il a également insisté sur le renforcement de la visibilité et de la communication de l’organisation. Le président a, par ailleurs, félicité le nouveau secrétaire général de l’UPA, Bahouaba Norbert Tankoano, ainsi que le président de l’Assemblée nationale du Tchad, élu à la tête du groupe africain de l’UIP. Le président du Sénat congolais a exprimé sa gratitude aux autorités togolaises pour leur solidarité et leur engagement ayant permis la tenue des présentes assises à Lomé, ainsi que le bon déroulement des célébrations du 50e anniversaire de l’UPA. Il a enfin remercié les délégations pour leur soutien à la RDC face à la crise sécuritaire et humanitaire dans l’Est du pays, avant de réaffirmer sa disponibilité à œuvrer au rayonnement de l’Union dans un esprit de fraternité et de solidarité. Créée en 1976 à Abidjan, en Côte d’Ivoire, l’UPA regroupe les parlements des Etats africains et œuvre au renforcement de la coopération interparlementaire, de la démocratie, de la paix et du développement sur le continent. ATOP/SED/JK

items.title: Violences meurtrières à Siguiri en Guinée: indignation et condamnation de Cellou Dalein Diallo
items.description: Sur les «événements tragiques» de Siguiri, provoqués par «l’interdiction brutale et insuffisamment préparée de l’exploitation artisanale de l’or» le leader de l’opposition guinéenne en exil, Cellou Dalein Diallo s’indigne, condamne et «exige l’ouverture d’une enquête indépendante et crédible afin de faire toute la lumière sur ces violences, d’identifier les responsables de cette tragédie et de les déférer devant les tribunaux.» «J’exprime ma profonde indignation et condamne fermement les violences meurtrières qui ont endeuillé de nombreuses familles à Siguiri et plongé toute la nation et beaucoup de pays voisins dans la tristesse. Ces événements tragiques interviennent dans un contexte de fortes tensions provoquées par l’interdiction brutale et insuffisamment préparée de l’exploitation artisanale de l’or, une activité qui fait vivre des milliers de familles de la région depuis des siècles. Une telle décision ne pouvait être appliquée sereinement sans une large sensibilisation des populations, l’implication des communautés locales et la mise en place de mesures d’accompagnement destinées à préserver la dignité et les intérêts de nos compatriotes ainsi que les relations de bon voisinage avec les pays de la sous-région. L’usage de la force en l’absence de ces préalables ne pouvait conduire qu’au désastre que nous déplorons aujourd’hui: des dizaines de morts et de blessés graves, d’importants dégâts matériels, des centaines d’arrestations, l’expulsion massive et brutale de ressortissants ouest-africains, au prix d’une grave dégradation de nos relations avec leurs pays d’origine. À cela s’ajoutent les poursuites injustifiées visant des centaines de citoyens, des dizaines d’élus locaux et d’administrateurs territoriaux. Face à cette situation qui humilie la nation, j’exige l’ouverture d’une enquête indépendante et crédible afin de faire toute la lumière sur ces violences, d’identifier les responsables de cette tragédie et de les déférer devant les tribunaux. J’adresse mes sincères condoléances aux familles des victimes, souhaite un prompt rétablissement aux blessés et exprime toute ma solidarité avec mes frères guinéens et ouest-africains touchés par cette folie meurtrière des autorités guinéennes.» Cellou Dalein Diallo L’article Violences meurtrières à Siguiri en Guinée: indignation et condamnation de Cellou Dalein Diallo est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: 86è session du comité exécutif de l’UPA : Bahouaba Norbert Tankoano élu nouveau secrétaire général
items.description: Lomé, 14 nov. (ATOP) – Bahouaba Norbert Tankoano a été élu nouveau secrétaire général de l’Union parlementaire africaine (UPA), le samedi 14 novembre à Lomé, à l’issue de la 86e session du Comité exécutif de l’organisation. Il est élu pour un mandat de quatre ans renouvelable. Plaçant son mandat sous le signe de l’unité continentale et de la rigueur dans l’action, le nouveau secrétaire général a réaffirmé sa volonté de servir tous les parlements membres, sans distinction. Il a notamment adressé un message aux six pays qui n’ont pas soutenu sa candidature, leur assurant qu’il exercera ses fonctions avec loyauté et impartialité, indépendamment de l’origine géographique ou de la langue des parlementaires. M.Tankoano a également salué les réalisations de son prédécesseur et pris acte des recommandations formulées au cours des travaux, notamment celles relatives à la redynamisation des parlements nationaux et à l’amélioration des ressources financières de l’organisation. Il a indiqué que les attentes exprimées à l’endroit de la présidence du Comité exécutif constitueront également des orientations pour le secrétariat général. Sa stratégie pour le développement de l’UPA repose sur quatre priorités interdépendantes. Il s’agit notamment de remobiliser les parlements membres qui se sont éloignés de l’organisation, de renforcer sa situation financière à travers le paiement régulier des cotisations, de diversifier ses activités par l’organisation de séminaires, d’ateliers et de conférences en dehors des sessions statutaires, et d’améliorer son rayonnement international grâce à une stratégie de communication renforcée. Le nouveau secrétaire général prendra officiellement fonction en janvier 2027. ATOP/SED/JK

items.title: “¡Enano!” o la historia de una agresión en Madrid
items.description: La era de la crueldad deja víctimas. La última ha sido un hombre curioso, inteligente, divertido y culto, una buena persona, llegado a Madrid para asistir al festival Eñe que se celebra estos días, hambriento siempre de conocer nuevos libros, autores y tendencias para atraerlos a Fuerteventura, donde se dedica a agitar la escena cultural. Paseaba Carlos (nombre ficticio, porque él prefiere mantener su anonimato) por la plaza de Callao, centro vital de esta ciudad hoy masificada, a veces enloquecida, cuando un hombre se le encaró. “¡Enano!”, le gritó mientras le palmeaba la cabeza. Después le tiró al suelo de una patada, lo que le fracturó el fémur. Hoy se recupera entre aparatos en la planta de traumatología de un hospital. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Les navires européens opérant dans la zone mauritanienne de pêche priés de rentrer ce soir au port de Nouadhibou après la fin de l’accord de pêche entre la Mauritanie et l’UE
items.description: La Garde côtière mauritanienne a publié une circulaire ordonnant la suspension des activités des navires de pêche de l'Union européenne dans la zone de pêche mauritanienne, à l'expiration du protocole d'application de l'accord de partenariat dans le domaine de la pêche entre la Mauritanie et l'Union européenne. Dans une circulaire publiée ce samedi 14 novembre, la Garde côtière a déclaré : que le protocole expire à 00 h 00, et a exigé que tous les navires de pêche européens opérant dans les eaux mauritaniennes cessent leurs activités et se dirigent vers le port de Nouadhibou avant cette date, afin d’accomplir les formalités administratives et maritimes nécessaires à leur sortie de la zone économique exclusive de la Mauritanie. La Garde côtière a averti que tout manquement à ces instructions serait sanctionné conformément à la législation en vigueur. L’accord de pêche entre la Mauritanie et l’Union européenne remonte à 1987, tandis que le protocole d’application actuel arrive à échéance sans que les deux parties ne soient parvenues à un accord sur un nouveau protocole, malgré les cycles de négociations qui se sont tenus au cours des derniers mois.

items.title: Troisième édition de la semaine du Maroc à Nouakchott du 16 au 22 novembre
items.description: Nouakchott va accueillir du 16 au 22 novembre prochain la troisième édition de la « Semaine du Maroc », à laquelle participent des institutions gouvernementales et des organismes économiques des deux pays, dans le but de faire connaître les opportunités d'échanges commerciaux et d'investissement entre la Mauritanie et le Maroc. Selon un communiqué de presse publié par les organisateurs de l’événement, celui-ci est organisé en collaboration avec l’ambassade du Maroc et l’association « Forum du Sud », en partenariat avec le ministère mauritanien du Commerce et du Tourisme et le ministère marocain de l’Industrie, de l’Investissement et de l’Économie numérique, ainsi qu’avec un certain nombre d’organismes et d’institutions économiques des deux pays. Le communiqué ajoute que le programme de la manifestation comprend des rencontres bilatérales entre hommes d’affaires et entreprises, mais aussi entre entreprises et organismes gouvernementaux, sans oublier des tables rondes consacrées aux perspectives de coopération économique entre les deux pays et aux grands projets qui renforcent leur partenariat. Cette semaine a pour objectif d’explorer les opportunités d’échanges commerciaux et d’investissement dans les secteurs de l’industrie, de la construction, des travaux publics, de l’énergie, de l’agroalimentaire, de l’agriculture, du secteur bancaire et des télécommunications. Le programme comprend également des présentations consacrées à la culture marocaine, à l’artisanat, à la gastronomie et aux produits locaux, ainsi que des soirées artistiques, musicales et poétiques tout au long de l’événement.

items.title: Enseignement supérieur en Afrique : l'UM6P, un modèle d'excellence à suivre ?
items.description: L'Afrique peut-elle former ses propres élites sans les envoyer étudier à l'étranger ? Au Maroc, l'Université Mohammed VI Polytechnique (UM6P) s'impose parmi les établissements africains les mieux classés à l'international. Recherche, intelligence artificielle, robotique, agriculture : l'université mise sur des formations de pointe pour répondre aux défis du continent. Mais cette excellence est-elle accessible à tous ? Et ce modèle peut-il être reproduit ailleurs en Afrique ? Sa Benjamin Traoré, professeur de droit public et directeur du programme Droit et Gouvernance à l'UM6P, est l'invité de Fatimata Wane dans le Journal de l'Afrique sur France 24.

items.title: Incivilité vs Téranga (Le billet de Omar DIOUF)
items.description: Un extrait de vidéo postée sur la page facebook du journaliste gabonais Freddy Koula Moussavou, a généré, mercredi, un vif échange d’incivilités entre internautes sénégalais. Des injures et des propos discourtois sont venus polluer le contenu de ce post du journaliste qui s’adressait à l’ancien président Macky Sall sur la télévision togolaise New World, en ces termes : « En parlant de double nationalité, mon père est à Matam, donc je viendrai chercher mon passeport sénégalais… » En quoi le président Sall avait répondu : « Ha oui ? Je suis également originaire de la région de Matam… ». Bref, actuellement en séjour à Dakar où se déroulent les Joj 2026, Freddy Koula Moussavou, voulait juste faire un clin d’œil en postant : « Ça tombe bien, j’y suis… au pays de la Téranga ». Mais le flot d’incivilités échangées entre internautes sénégalais, a fini par étaler toute la grossièreté affichée par certains de nos compatriotes sur les réseaux sociaux, sur tous les sujets, même le plus banal. La belle « Téranga » dont nous nous gargarisons ne se reflète plus dans nos relations entre concitoyens. La partisannerie est venue bafouer toutes ces valeurs que nos ancêtres ont forgées jusque-là. Notre Boîte de Pandore est bien ouverte. omar.diouf@lesoleil.sn

items.description: La librairie Al Kitab de Mutuelleville, à Tunis, accueille l'historien Abdelhamid Larguèche ce dimanche 15 novembre 2026 à partir de 10h30. Cette rencontre littéraire est dédiée à la présentation et à la dédicace de ses deux dernières parutions, intitulées « Les héritiers du silence » et « La voix de la braise ». Cet événement culturel offrira au public et aux passionnés d'histoire et de littérature l'opportunité d'échanger directement avec l'auteur autour de la genèse, des thématiques et de l'écriture de ces deux nouvelles œuvres. La rencontre se déroulera au sein même de l'espace de la librairie située à Mutuelleville. items.title: El cantante Gabito Ballesteros, arrestado tras cantar un corrido en Querétaro
items.description: El cantante Gabito Ballesteros fue arrestado en la madrugada de este sábado después de haber interpretado la canción AMG en la Feria Internacional Ganadera de Querétaro, en el municipio de El Marqués. El artista fue detenido por la policía estatal y puesto a disposición de la FGR, según el Registro Nacional de Detenciones. La Fiscalía federal ha confirmado que lo investiga, junto a otros cuatro hombres, por portación de un arma de fuego de uso exclusivo del ejército y por desobediencia y resistencia de particulares. Los organizadores del evento han afirmado que suspendieron el concierto de Ballesteros porque interpretó “en dos ocasiones temas no autorizados que hacen apología del delito”. Las autoridades de México emprendieron el año pasado una cruzada contra los narcocorridos que llevó a algunos Gobiernos locales, como el de Querétaro, a prohibir su reproducción en espacios públicos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Coyah-Kindia : les trafics sur la RN1 paralysés après le renversement d’un camion-remorque à Labota
items.description: La circulation est fortement perturbée sur la Route nationale numéro 1 (RN1), au niveau de Labota, au PK 40, dans la sous-préfecture de Mambia, préfecture de Kindia, à la suite du renversement d’un camion-remorque en pleine chaussée. Survenu aux environs de 17 heures, l’accident a provoqué un blocage presque total du trafic sur cet axe stratégique reliant Conakry à l’intérieur du pays. Des dizaines, voire des centaines de véhicules sont immobilisés de part et d’autre du lieu de l’accident, occasionnant un embouteillage particulièrement impressionnant. Après plusieurs heures d’attente, la situation reste toujours difficile pour les usagers. Depuis près de cinq heures, automobilistes, transporteurs et voyageurs sont contraints de patienter, dans l’espoir d’une reprise normale de la circulation. Sur les lieux, les éléments de la gendarmerie routière sont mobilisés pour tenter de fluidifier le trafic et trouver une issue à cette situation qui pénalise fortement les usagers de la route. Pour l’heure, les circonstances exactes de l’accident et le bilan d’éventuels blessés ne sont pas encore connus. Ce nouvel incident remet en lumière la vulnérabilité de la RN1, un axe routier stratégique où le renversement d’un poids lourd suffit à provoquer une paralysie majeure de la circulation, avec des conséquences importantes pour les milliers d’usagers qui l’empruntent quotidiennement.
